**PR #1506**: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/1506

Agreed on why this is cool — and the sharper version of it is that these actions address the user **by name**, not by entity ID. Entity IDs derive from the name, so `switch.all_locks_sarah_chen_enabled` moves the moment someone is renamed and any automation holding it silently stops working. Name-addressed actions survive that, which is what makes REST automation against this actually durable rather than just possible.

`enable_user` routes through the coordinator's toggle, so it inherits the refusal of a credential-less user and the repair-issue clearing. That refusal is a bare `Exception`, so I translate it — otherwise it surfaces as an internal error rather than the caller's mistake. `disable_user` is unconditional and **keeps the credential**, so re-enabling restores it; mutation M3 pins that by making disable clear the PIN and confirming a test catches it.

2301 passing, 100% coverage, all hooks, three mutations killed.

**One correction to the parity claim, which I checked rather than assumed.** I enumerated the writable per-user surfaces: `name`, `pin`, `enabled`. Two gaps existed, not one — and after this PR, **renaming is still not reachable by action.**

I left it out deliberately. A rename moves every one of that user's entity IDs, and per this project's own notes the recorder follows a rename only when the new name isn't already taken — so it has failure modes these two don't. It deserves its own change rather than being tacked on.

So: after #1506, everything the UI can do per user is reachable by service *except* rename. Want that next?

Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

## Proposed change

Four actions that address a **person by name**, closing the gap between what the dashboard can do per user and what a service (and therefore REST) can.

```yaml
lock_code_manager.enable_user:     config_entry + name
lock_code_manager.disable_user:    config_entry + name
lock_code_manager.set_condition:   config_entry + name + entity_id
lock_code_manager.clear_condition: config_entry + name
```

**Addressed by name, not entity ID or slot number** — which is the point rather than a convenience. Entity IDs derive from the user's name, so `switch.all_locks_sarah_chen_enabled` moves the moment somebody is renamed and an automation holding it silently stops working. A slot number is worse: it stays valid and comes to address *whoever occupies that slot later*, so the automation keeps working on the wrong person.

### enable_user / disable_user

**Enable** goes through the coordinator's toggle rather than writing `enabled` itself, inheriting that path's rules: it refuses a user holding no credential, and clears the `pin_required` repair issue raised when that last happened. That refusal is a bare `Exception`, translated here so it reaches the caller as their problem rather than as an internal error.

**Disable** is unconditional and **keeps the credential in the configuration**, so enabling again restores it without anybody having to remember what it was.

### set_condition / clear_condition

Same shape as `set_credential` before them: `set_slot_condition` and `clear_slot_condition` keep working **unchanged** and now log a warning naming their replacement.

`clear_condition` removes the gate without disabling anybody — a user with no condition is one whose credential simply always applies.

The deprecation warning takes its reason as an argument rather than restating one message for both pairs, because they're deprecated for different reasons: the usercode pair wrote past the configuration, this pair addresses bookkeeping.

## Type of change

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.content:
# Integrations That Cannot Currently Be Supported

Many lock integrations don't yet have Lock Code Manager providers, but could potentially be
added in the future (see [[Adding a Provider|Adding-a-Provider]]). The integrations listed
on this page are different - they **cannot** be supported due to fundamental limitations in
their underlying libraries or protocols.

The Home Assistant lock platform only requires lock/unlock operations. User code management
is optional, and these integrations don't expose it.

## ESPHome

**Status:** Not possible

The ESPHome lock component only supports lock/unlock/open commands. There is no API for
managing user codes on keypads.

**What would need to change:** ESPHome would need to implement user code management in its
firmware and expose it through the ESPHome API. This would be a significant feature addition
to the ESPHome project.

## Yale / August

**Status:** Not possible

Four integrations exist for Yale/August locks:

| Integration | Library | Notes |
| ----------- | ------- | ----- |
| `august` | `yalexs` | Can READ PINs but cannot create/update/delete them |
| `yale` | `yalexs` | Same library as `august` - can READ PINs but cannot manage them |

|---|---|---|---|
{ENTRY}

action: lock_code_manager.enable_user

  config_entry_title: All Locks
  name: Sarah Chen

Turn a person off and clear their credential from the entry's locks.

**Their credential stays in the configuration**, so enabling them again restores it — nobody has to remember what the code was. To remove the person altogether, use [`delete_user`](#delete_user); to remove just the credential, [`clear_credential`](#clear_credential).

**No, that page was not accurate** — and it was wrong about the exact thing this session shipped.

It said **"ESPHome — Status: Not possible"**, which since 5.3.0 sends precisely the wrong user away. LCM still can't be a *provider* for ESPHome (it can't push a PIN onto the device), but an ESPHome keypad is now fully supported from the other direction — the keypad reports the code, `use_credential` checks it, and a config entry needs no locks at all.

I rewrote that section to draw the distinction, retitled the page from "Integrations That Cannot Currently Be Supported" to **"Integrations With No Provider"** (the old title contradicted its own content), and added a note up front that "no provider" ≠ "no support."

**The Yale/August section I left alone.** Those are claims about `yalexs` internals — that `async_get_pins()` exists but there are no create/update/delete methods. `yalexs` isn't installed here, so I can't verify them, and I'm not going to endorse or "correct" external-library specifics I haven't checked.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). def test_every_translation_matches_the_strings_it_translates() -> None:
    """
    A string added to one file and not the other ships untranslated.

    ``strings.json`` is what Home Assistant uploads for translation and
    ``translations/en.json`` is what it actually renders for an English
    install, so a string that reaches only the first is one nobody sees.
    The whole document is compared, not just the entity names: the config
    flow reads its field labels from here too, and a rename that lands in
    one file leaves the other naming a key that no longer exists.
    """
    root = (

        / "custom_components"

    strings = json.loads((root / "strings.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    english = json.loads(
        (root / "translations" / "en.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    )

    install, so a string that reaches only the first is one nobody sees.
    The whole document is compared, not just the entity names: the config
    flow reads its field labels from here too, and a rename that lands in
    one file leaves the other naming a key that no longer exists.
    """
    root = (
        pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
        / "custom_components"
        / "lock_code_manager"
    )
    strings = json.loads((root / "strings.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    english = json.loads(
        (root / "translations" / "en.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    )

    assert strings == english

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.text:
Found the blocker, and it's worth your call rather than my guess.

**Line 606:** `_renderCodeDisplayMode(slot, mode, isUnmanaged && !isEditing)` — editing in `lock-codes-card` is offered **only for unmanaged slots**. Those are codes sitting on the lock that LCM doesn't manage, so by definition they have no LCM user, no name, and no config-entry slot. `set_credential` can't address them: it requires a user name in an entry.

So the two pairs aren't symmetrical:

- **Conditions mirror cleanly.** `slot-card` is a per-user card and already knows the name, so `set_condition`/`clear_condition` are a straight swap.
- **Usercodes don't.** The only caller of `set_usercode`/`clear_usercode` is the unmanaged-slot editor, which is precisely the case the name-addressed command cannot express.

questions.question: `lock-codes-card` edits only *unmanaged* slots, which have no user to name. What should happen to that websocket pair?

options.label: Keep it, renamed for what it is (Recommended)
options.description: Remove the services, mirror the condition pair, and keep a device-level websocket command renamed to something honest like `write_unmanaged_code` / `clear_unmanaged_code`. The card keeps its feature. The escape hatch survives only where it is the entire point — fixing a stray code LCM does not manage — rather than as a general-purpose write.

options.label: Drop unmanaged editing from the card
options.description: Remove the websocket pair and the card's edit affordance, so no device-level write survives anywhere. Cleanest boundary, but users lose the ability to clear a stray code from the dashboard and have to use the lock's own app or the unmanaged sweep.

options.label: Make the card adopt the slot first
options.description: Replace editing with an 'adopt this code' flow: turn the unmanaged slot into a real LCM user, then write through set_credential. Most coherent with the config-level model, but it is a new feature with its own naming and allocation questions — much bigger than this PR.

            # walk back over decorators/comments attached to it
            while start and (lines[start-1].startswith("@")

content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.text:
**PR 1 is up: #1507** → `v6` — https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/1507

Twelve services remain, four gone, and the websocket commands renamed to match. 2279 passing, 100% coverage, all hooks green including the frontend build (the rebuilt bundle is committed).

**The thing worth your attention** is the `write_unmanaged_code` decision you picked, because investigating it changed what the PR could be. The lock-codes card's editor is gated on `isUnmanaged && !isEditing` — it edits *only* slots holding codes no LCM user owns. Those have no name, so `set_credential` can't address them at all. Keeping a device-level write there isn't a hole in the model; it's the card's entire purpose, and the new name says so.

Two process notes:

I made a mess partway through and backed out. My first pass deleted test functions with heuristic block boundaries, which swallowed a block of module-level constants and left two `@parametrize` decorators orphaned onto unrelated tests — which would have silently injected parameters into them. I restored the file from HEAD and redid it with AST-derived spans (`node.lineno` plus `decorator_list`), which is exact. Worth flagging because I also reported "restored and verified" once when my insert had silently no-oped; the second attempt asserts the content is actually present.

Three tests used `set_slot_condition` only as a *vehicle* to reach unrelated behavior — a wrong-domain entry, the settle timeout. Those moved to `set_condition` and got simpler, since they no longer look up a slot number to do it.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

questions.question: Removing the deprecated event makes keypad uses on *unmanaged* slots invisible — it was the only thing carrying them. What should v6 do?

options.label: Accept the loss (Recommended)
options.description: Lock Code Manager announces uses of credentials it manages; a code it does not manage is the lock integration's business. zwave_js, ZHA and Matter all fire their own notification events, so that signal is still available — just not through LCM. Simplest, and consistent with 'a provider is a credential store'.

options.label: Widen the unified event to carry them
options.description: Fire `credential_used` for unattributed uses too, with no name. This breaks a deliberate contract: the payload is documented as five fields always present and never empty, specifically so consumers need no key tests or null checks. Every existing consumer would have to start checking.

options.label: Add a separate unattributed-use event
options.description: A new event for uses LCM cannot pin to a user, keeping the unified event's strict payload intact. Preserves the capability honestly, but it is a new public surface to design, document and support — bigger than this PR.

content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

            # the name text entity below: that entity can be disabled, and it

content.description: Constants + async_validate_credential + ValidationResult + unit tests, TDD. Precedence: most restrictive wins (user_disabled > condition_not_met).

content.description: providers/reader.py subclassing VirtualLock, non-lock-domain dispatch in resolve_provider_class_for_entity, state listener, tests.

content.subject: Task 3: Config flow readers selector
content.description: Optional readers field (sensor/text) on user + options steps, merge into CONF_LOCKS, at_least_one error, strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 4: validate_code service
content.description: Service registration with SupportsResponse.OPTIONAL, multi-entry handling, services.yaml + strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 5: Property test validation ⇔ active sensor
content.description: Hypothesis property test in tests/properties/ asserting validation agrees with active binary sensor.

content.subject: Task 6: Reader E2E + full suite verification
content.description: Full-stack reader E2E incl. mixed entry, websocket/strategy tolerance check, full pytest + prek, 100% coverage.

content.description: Keypad/PIN-only wiki page (no RFID yet, decided 2026-08-25) and #1414 comment describing both options.

content.subject: Fix final-review criticals and importants
content.description: Critical 1 shared-instance multi-entry; Critical 2 ATTR_STATE cleartext; Imp 3 stale revalidation; Imp 4 diagnostics; Imp 5 normalization; Minor precedence duplication.

content.description: Retitle for use_credential + unified event + blueprint; rewrite body (currently describes validate_code as a pure query, which is two designs stale).

content.subject: Update README for shipped items
content.description: Add credential_used.yaml to the automation-blueprint list; add a feature bullet for validating codes entered outside LCM-managed locks. Direction/roadmap stays out.

content.description: Currently documents validate_code as a pure query with no events. Needs use_credential (source/target required), the unified event, and the new blueprint. Staged unpushed until merge.

content.description: docs/2026-08-25-session-handoff-1414.md describes the design as of stages 1-5 planned; update to what actually shipped.

content.description: Fix agent a55956239d83904a5 is applying the three Important findings (declaration exit, orphan pruning, misleading copy) plus the registryless-entity minor. Run /code-review on 1489 once it commits and pushes.

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

**Answer: it's migration-only in production, and the docstring saying otherwise is stale.** Three separate things wear that name:

- **Migration** (`user_migration.py`, `__init__.py:191–232`) — converting v2/v3 slot-keyed configs. Legitimate.

- **Websocket payload** (`websocket.py:458, 697`) — `slots` as a wire-format key for the card. Unrelated to stored config, just confusingly named.

So the acceptance path in `from_mapping` is fed by migration and **by tests** — `BASE_CONFIG` and most fixtures use the slot-keyed shape. That's tests exercising an input shape production no longer emits, which is worth its own cleanup, not this PR. Let me finish this one:

    A lock in the entry gets the use recorded on the slot's event entity.

    The recording is the event entity's own reading of the unified event,

---

    A cover is not a lock, is not in the entry, and could never be named by
    anything the entry knows -- and it is still alice's credential being
    used, so her entity is where that belongs. Only the unified event
    fires: the deprecated lock-shaped one would have to claim a from/to
    transition that never happened.
    """
    unified = async_capture_events(hass, BUS_EVENT_CREDENTIAL_USED)
    deprecated = async_capture_events(hass, EVENT_LOCK_STATE_CHANGED)
    before = hass.states.get(VALIDATE_EVENT_ENTITY_ID)

    await _call_use_credential(

    )
    await hass.async_block_till_done()

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. # Breaking change

**`lock_code_manager_lock_state_changed` no longer fires.** Use `lock_code_manager_credential_used`, which has fired alongside it since 5.2.0. Automations still listening for the old event will never trigger.

The payloads differ. The unified event names the **person**: `name`, `config_entry_id`, `config_entry_title`, `source`, `target`, `credential_type`, `operation`. Mapping the fields you are most likely using:

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `entity_id` (the lock) | `target` — and `source`, equal to it when a lock observed the use |
| `code_slot` | *(gone — the event names the user, not their slot number)* |
| `code_slot_name` | `name` |
| `from` / `to` | `operation` (`lock`, `unlock`, `unknown`) |
| `action_text`, `notification_source`, `extra_data`, `state` | *(no equivalent)* |

**A keypad use on a slot Lock Code Manager does not manage is now announced nowhere.** The old event fired for every slot a lock reported; the unified event names whose credential was used, and there is no user to name here, so it stays silent by design. If you relied on that, listen to your lock integration's own notification event instead — `zwave_js_event`, ZHA's, and Matter's all still fire.

## Proposed change

Second of two PRs onto `v6`, stacked on #1507.

Nothing inside the integration read the deprecated event: the per-slot event entity has recorded off the unified one alone since 5.3.0. It existed purely for consumers.

Removing it made a chain of things dead, which is the bulk of this diff:

- Its payload was the **only** consumer of `action_text` and `source_data` — two parameters all six providers were computing and passing. Both are removed from `async_fire_code_slot_event`, along with `_serialize_source_data` and the dead locals in ZHA that only fed them.
- Nine constants named payload fields nothing else publishes: `ATTR_ACTION_TEXT`, `ATTR_NOTIFICATION_SOURCE`, `ATTR_EXTRA_DATA`, `ATTR_CODE_SLOT_NAME`, `ATTR_FROM`, `ATTR_TO`, `ATTR_LCM_CONFIG_ENTRY_ID`, `ATTR_LOCK_CONFIG_ENTRY_ID`, and `EVENT_LOCK_STATE_CHANGED`. Each was verified unreferenced across production, tests and the frontend before deletion.

### Tests

Provider tests that used the removed event as their observable now **spy on `async_fire_code_slot_event`**. That is the behaviour they were actually asserting — what the provider does with a notification — and it no longer depends on whether an attributable user happens to exist in the fixture. Two exceptions kept a bus listener because a spy would miss the point: `test_borrowed` catches a *second, leaked* provider instance re-reporting, and the zwave-js-ui E2E asserts the whole chain through to the event entity.

Four `source_data` tests were deleted; they tested a parameter that no longer exists.

## Type of change

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (which adds functionality)
- [x] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information

- This PR fixes or closes issue: fixes #1504

class ConfigSubentry:
    """Container for a configuration subentry."""

    data: MappingProxyType[str, Any]
    subentry_id: str = field(default_factory=ulid_util.ulid_now)
    subentry_type: str
    title: str
    unique_id: str | None

    def as_dict(self) -> ConfigSubentryDataWithId:
        """Return dictionary version of this subentry."""
        return {
            "data": dict(self.data),
            "subentry_id": self.subentry_id,
            "subentry_type": self.subentry_type,
            "title": self.title,
            "unique_id": self.unique_id,
        }


class ConfigEntry[_DataT = Any]:

content.description: Add credential_used.yaml to the automation-blueprint list; add a feature bullet for validating codes entered outside LCM-managed locks. Direction/roadmap stays out.

content.description: #1485, #1486, #1487 — read each description against its actual final diff, not against the agent's report. #1487 especially: title and body predate the operation field, credential-type event_types, and the limiter input.

content.description: Fix agent a55956239d83904a5 is applying the three Important findings (declaration exit, orphan pruning, misleading copy) plus the registryless-entity minor. Run /code-review on 1489 once it commits and pushes.

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

# A slot is a subentry (v6)

Design proposal. Local only — `docs/` is gitignored.

Verified against `homeassistant` 2026.8 as installed in `.venv`. Every API named
here was read in that source, not recalled.

## The idea

One Lock Code Manager config entry holds many users. Today they live in a dict on
the entry (`users: {name: {...}}`) with a side table numbering them
(`slot_assignment: {identity: slot}`). Home Assistant has a first-class shape for
"one entry, many things": **subentries**.

**A slot becomes a subentry.** The entry stays the thing that holds locks; each
user becomes a `ConfigSubentry` under it.

### Why this fits better than it might look

The grouping already exists. `entity.py::build_slot_device_info` gives every slot
its **own device**, identified `{entry_id}|{slot_num}`, named `{entry title} {user}`,
carrying that user's `name`, `pin`, `enabled`, `active` and `credential_used`
entities. Subentries are not a new concept being imposed — they are the concept
already in use, currently expressed by hand.

Home Assistant supports exactly this:

| Need | API (verified) |
|---|---|
| The container | `ConfigSubentry(data, subentry_id, subentry_type, title, unique_id)` |
| Add / remove / edit | `async_add_subentry`, `async_remove_subentry`, `async_update_subentry` on `ConfigEntries` |
| A UI flow to create one | `ConfigFlow.async_get_supported_subentry_types` → `ConfigSubentryFlow` |
| Editing an existing one | `ConfigSubentryFlow` with `SOURCE_RECONFIGURE` (`_reconfigure_subentry_id`) |
| Binding entities | `async_add_entities(..., config_subentry_id=...)` |
| Binding the device | `DeviceEntry.config_subentry_id` |

`async_add_subentry` is a plain public method, so **services can create subentries
directly** without going through a flow. That is what keeps `add_user` working.

## The central decision: what identifies a slot's entities

This is the one choice that decides how big the change is, and it should be made
deliberately rather than fallen into.

Today: `build_slot_unique_id(entry_id, slot_num, key)` → `{entry_id}|{slot}|{key}`,
and the device is `{entry_id}|{slot_num}`.

### Option A — keep slot_num in identifiers, add subentries alongside

Entities keep their unique IDs. Subentries become the storage shape and the UI
affordance; `config_subentry_id` is attached to entities and devices.

- **No entity IDs move.** Nothing in anyone's dashboard or automations breaks.
- Migration writes subentries from `users` + `slot_assignment` and stops there.
- The slot number stays the durable key, which is what
  `project_slot_number_is_two_keys_fused` concluded was correct: the key denotes a
  credential position, and reuse is right.

### Option B — move identifiers onto `subentry_id`

`subentry_id` is a ULID, never reused, immune to renames *and* to renumbering.

- Fixes the "entity IDs derive from a mutable name" problem at the root.
- **But it renames every entity in every installation.** 5.0 already did that once
  (`project_lcm_5_0_0_released`, the rename notification, the recorder rules in
  `project_ha_recorder_rename_semantics`). Doing it again buys durability nobody
  has asked for.
- It also contradicts the settled position that the slot number *is* the identity
  of a credential position.

**Recommendation: Option A.** Take the storage and UI benefits; leave identifiers
alone. Revisit B only if renaming becomes a real reported problem.

## Shape

```python
ConfigSubentry(
    subentry_type="slot",
    title="Sarah Chen",          # the user's name; what the UI lists
    unique_id=str(slot_num),     # unique within the entry
    data={
        "slot": 3,               # the credential position
        "pin": "1234",
        "enabled": True,
        "condition": "calendar.bookings",   # optional
    },
)
```

`EntryConfig` keeps its current external surface — `users`, `assignment`,
`name_for`, `slot`, `has_slot` — and reads from `entry.subentries` instead of
`entry.data`. Every caller above the config layer is unaffected. That is the whole
point of `EntryConfig` existing.

`locks` and `availability_entities` stay on the entry: they belong to the entry,
not to any one user.

## Keeping the services working

Requirement, not a nice-to-have.

| Action | After |
|---|---|
| `add_user` | allocate a slot as today, then `async_add_subentry(...)` |
| `delete_user` | `async_remove_subentry(entry, subentry_id)` |
| `set_credential` / `clear_credential` | `async_update_subentry(...)` with new `data` |
| `enable_user` / `disable_user` | same |
| `set_condition` / `clear_condition` | same |

The name-addressed resolution added in 5.4.0 (`_stored_user`, `_slot_for_user`)
becomes a lookup over `entry.subentries.values()` matching `identity(title)`. One
helper changes; the six actions above do not.

**Trap:** `async_update_subentry` replaces `data` wholesale. `SlotEntityCoordinator`
already learned this lesson for entry data — `_write_config_fields` coalesces
writes because "the update listener has not yet refreshed `runtime_data.config`
between two consecutive writes, leading the second write to drop the first". The
same coalescing has to survive the move, or `set_credential` immediately followed
by `enable_user` will drop the PIN.

## The UI, and the bonus

### What exists today

`add-user-card.ts` hand-builds a form and calls `lock_code_manager.add_user`. It
hand-builds it because **custom cards cannot use Home Assistant's `ha-*` form
components** — they are not registered for custom elements, and an unregistered
`ha-*` renders as nothing at all, invisibly, with no DOM test able to catch it
(`feedback_dashboard_cards_cannot_use_ha_form_components`; it shipped twice).

So the bonus is worth real points: if the card can hand the user to Home
Assistant's own subentry dialog, **Home Assistant renders the form** and the whole
class of bug disappears, along with the hand-built card.

### What I verified

Subentry flows are driven over **REST**, not websocket:
`/api/config/config_entries/subentries/flow`. The websocket API only exposes
`subentries/list`, `subentries/update`, `subentries/delete` — no flow driving.

That matters: a card **cannot** drive a subentry flow itself without rendering the
forms, which is the thing we are trying to escape. So the bonus depends entirely on
opening Home Assistant's *own* dialog.

### Options, honestly ranked

1. **Fire `show-dialog`.** The frontend's dialog manager listens for a `show-dialog`
   event carrying `dialogTag` / `dialogImport` / `dialogParams`. `dialogImport` is a
   function returning a dynamic import of a frontend-internal module, which a custom
   card has no import path for. It *may* work with `dialogTag` alone when the element
   is already defined — but that depends on whether the user has visited a page that
   loaded it, which is not a contract.
   **Status: unverified. Prototype before promising.** This is exactly the shape of
   claim `feedback_read_the_framework_before_claiming_a_limit` says to test rather
   than assert — in both directions.

2. **Navigate to the integration page.** Reliable, uses only public navigation, and
   lands the user on Home Assistant's own subentry list with its Add button. Leaves
   the dashboard, which is worse UX but is honest and cannot break.

3. **Keep the custom card, backed by `add_user`.** Zero risk, zero benefit; the
   hand-built form stays and so does its failure mode.

**Recommendation:** spend a timebox on (1) with a real dashboard, because the payoff
is deleting a card and a class of bug. Fall back to (2), which is a small, safe
change. Do not ship (1) on the strength of it working in a unit test — this failure
mode is invisible to DOM tests by construction.

Independently of the bonus, the subentry flow should exist and be good, because it
is what the Integrations page will show.

## Migration

Entry version 4 → 5.

For each user in `users`: create a subentry with its assigned slot, then clear
`users` and `slot_assignment` from entry data.

Then re-point the existing registry rows, which is the part that must not be
half-done:

- Every slot device: set `config_subentry_id`.
- Every slot entity: set `config_subentry_id`.

Both keep their current identifiers under Option A, so nothing renames.

**A user with no slot number is dropped**, exactly as `EntryConfig.__post_init__`
already drops them from `_by_slot` — "inventing one would put this user's code on a
credential index somebody else may hold". The migration should log each one by name
rather than silently discarding it.

**Rollback:** `project_v3_migration_one_way_door` applies again. There is no
code-level downgrade; recovery is a Home Assistant backup restore. Say so in the
release notes *before* release, not after.

## What I have not resolved

Genuine open questions, not rhetorical ones:

1. **Does the options flow survive?** Today it edits locks *and* users in one form.
   Users move to subentry flows; locks stay in options. That splits one screen into
   two places, which may be better (each thing where it belongs) or worse (two
   places to look). Worth deciding before building, because the answer changes what
   the options flow is for.

2. **Does `subentry_type` need to be more than `"slot"`?** One type is enough today.
   If a future member type appears (`project_credential_mgmt_refactor`), a second
   type is additive — but naming it `"slot"` now means the vocabulary says slot when
   #1480 concluded the domain word is *member*. `"user"` may age better.

3. **What does the dashboard strategy do with subentries?** It builds views from
   config today. Subentries do not change the data it reads through `EntryConfig`,
   but the per-user device is now a subentry device, and HA groups those differently
   on the device page. Needs a look, not a guess.

4. **Slot capacity and allocation** are unchanged in mechanism, but allocation
   currently reads `len(config.users)`. That becomes `len(entry.subentries)` — check
   there is no path that counts one while writing the other.

## Sequencing

Each step is independently mergeable and leaves the branch working.

1. **Subentry flow + `async_get_supported_subentry_types`.** Adds the UI affordance;
   nothing reads subentries yet. Smallest possible first step, and it makes the
   flow reviewable on its own.
2. **`EntryConfig` reads subentries; migration v4 → v5.** The load-bearing change.
   Everything above the config layer should be untouched — if it is not, the
   abstraction was leakier than believed, and that is worth knowing here rather
   than in step 4.
3. **Services write subentries.** Mechanical once step 2 lands, given the
   name-resolution helper is already centralised.
4. **Entities and devices bind via `config_subentry_id`.**
5. **Frontend:** prototype the dialog hand-off; then either delete the add-user
   card or keep it pointed at `add_user`.

Steps 1–4 are backend and testable with the existing suite at 100%. Step 5 is where
the risk lives, and it is deliberately last so that a failure there does not block
the model change.

1	# A slot is a subentry (v6)
2	
3	Design proposal. Local only — `docs/` is gitignored.
4	
5	Verified against `homeassistant` 2026.8 as installed in `.venv`. Every API named
6	here was read in that source, not recalled.
7	
8	## The idea
9	
10	One Lock Code Manager config entry holds many users. Today they live in a dict on
11	the entry (`users: {name: {...}}`) with a side table numbering them
12	(`slot_assignment: {identity: slot}`). Home Assistant has a first-class shape for
13	"one entry, many things": **subentries**.
14	
15	**A slot becomes a subentry.** The entry stays the thing that holds locks; each
16	user becomes a `ConfigSubentry` under it.
17	
18	### Why this fits better than it might look
19	
20	The grouping already exists. `entity.py::build_slot_device_info` gives every slot
21	its **own device**, identified `{entry_id}|{slot_num}`, named `{entry title} {user}`,
22	carrying that user's `name`, `pin`, `enabled`, `active` and `credential_used`
23	entities. Subentries are not a new concept being imposed — they are the concept
24	already in use, currently expressed by hand.
25	
26	Home Assistant supports exactly this:
27	
28	| Need | API (verified) |
29	|---|---|
30	| The container | `ConfigSubentry(data, subentry_id, subentry_type, title, unique_id)` |
31	| Add / remove / edit | `async_add_subentry`, `async_remove_subentry`, `async_update_subentry` on `ConfigEntries` |
32	| A UI flow to create one | `ConfigFlow.async_get_supported_subentry_types` → `ConfigSubentryFlow` |
33	| Editing an existing one | `ConfigSubentryFlow` with `SOURCE_RECONFIGURE` (`_reconfigure_subentry_id`) |
34	| Binding entities | `async_add_entities(..., config_subentry_id=...)` |
35	| Binding the device | `DeviceEntry.config_subentry_id` |
36	
37	`async_add_subentry` is a plain public method, so **services can create subentries
38	directly** without going through a flow. That is what keeps `add_user` working.
39	
40	## The central decision: what identifies a slot's entities
41	
42	This is the one choice that decides how big the change is, and it should be made
43	deliberately rather than fallen into.
44	
45	Today: `build_slot_unique_id(entry_id, slot_num, key)` → `{entry_id}|{slot}|{key}`,
46	and the device is `{entry_id}|{slot_num}`.
47	
48	### Option A — keep slot_num in identifiers, add subentries alongside
49	
50	Entities keep their unique IDs. Subentries become the storage shape and the UI
51	affordance; `config_subentry_id` is attached to entities and devices.
52	
53	- **No entity IDs move.** Nothing in anyone's dashboard or automations breaks.
54	- Migration writes subentries from `users` + `slot_assignment` and stops there.
55	- The slot number stays the durable key, which is what
56	  `project_slot_number_is_two_keys_fused` concluded was correct: the key denotes a
57	  credential position, and reuse is right.
58	
59	### Option B — move identifiers onto `subentry_id`
60	
61	`subentry_id` is a ULID, never reused, immune to renames *and* to renumbering.
62	
63	- Fixes the "entity IDs derive from a mutable name" problem at the root.
64	- **But it renames every entity in every installation.** 5.0 already did that once
65	  (`project_lcm_5_0_0_released`, the rename notification, the recorder rules in
66	  `project_ha_recorder_rename_semantics`). Doing it again buys durability nobody
67	  has asked for.
68	- It also contradicts the settled position that the slot number *is* the identity
69	  of a credential position.
70	
71	**Recommendation: Option A.** Take the storage and UI benefits; leave identifiers
72	alone. Revisit B only if renaming becomes a real reported problem.
73	
74	## Shape
75	
76	`subentry_type` is **`"user"`**, not `"slot"` and not `"member"`. A subentry holds a
77	*person* — their name, credential, enabled state and condition. "Member" is the
78	other axis entirely: `EntryConfig.member()` took a **lock's** registry entry, and a
79	member is "an entity this entry keeps credentials on", which is what #1480's
80	`CONF_LOCKS` → `CONF_MEMBERS` rename is about. Users and members are the two sides
81	of the entry, and a subentry is a user.
82	
83	`"user"` also matches the vocabulary already in the service surface — `add_user`,
84	`delete_user`, `enable_user`, `disable_user` — so nothing has to be learned twice.
85	
86	```python
87	ConfigSubentry(
88	    subentry_type="user",
89	    title="Sarah Chen",          # the user's name; what the UI lists
90	    unique_id=str(slot_num),     # unique within the entry
91	    data={
92	        "slot": 3,               # the credential position
93	        "pin": "1234",
94	        "enabled": True,
95	        "condition": "calendar.bookings",   # optional
96	    },
97	)
98	```
99	
100	`EntryConfig` keeps its current external surface — `users`, `assignment`,
101	`name_for`, `slot`, `has_slot` — and reads from `entry.subentries` instead of
102	`entry.data`. Every caller above the config layer is unaffected. That is the whole
103	point of `EntryConfig` existing.
104	
105	`locks` and `availability_entities` stay on the entry: they belong to the entry,
106	not to any one user.
107	
108	## Keeping the services working
109	
110	Requirement, not a nice-to-have.
111	
112	| Action | After |
113	|---|---|
114	| `add_user` | allocate a slot as today, then `async_add_subentry(...)` |
115	| `delete_user` | `async_remove_subentry(entry, subentry_id)` |
116	| `set_credential` / `clear_credential` | `async_update_subentry(...)` with new `data` |
117	| `enable_user` / `disable_user` | same |
118	| `set_condition` / `clear_condition` | same |
119	
120	The name-addressed resolution added in 5.4.0 (`_stored_user`, `_slot_for_user`)
121	becomes a lookup over `entry.subentries.values()` matching `identity(title)`. One
122	helper changes; the six actions above do not.
123	
124	**Trap:** `async_update_subentry` replaces `data` wholesale. `SlotEntityCoordinator`
125	already learned this lesson for entry data — `_write_config_fields` coalesces
126	writes because "the update listener has not yet refreshed `runtime_data.config`
127	between two consecutive writes, leading the second write to drop the first". The
128	same coalescing has to survive the move, or `set_credential` immediately followed
129	by `enable_user` will drop the PIN.
130	
131	## The UI, and the bonus
132	
133	### What exists today
134	
135	`add-user-card.ts` hand-builds a form and calls `lock_code_manager.add_user`. It
136	hand-builds it because **custom cards cannot use Home Assistant's `ha-*` form
137	components** — they are not registered for custom elements, and an unregistered
138	`ha-*` renders as nothing at all, invisibly, with no DOM test able to catch it
139	(`feedback_dashboard_cards_cannot_use_ha_form_components`; it shipped twice).
140	
141	So the bonus is worth real points: if the card can hand the user to Home
142	Assistant's own subentry dialog, **Home Assistant renders the form** and the whole
143	class of bug disappears, along with the hand-built card.
144	
145	### What I verified
146	
147	Subentry flows are driven over **REST**, not websocket:
148	`/api/config/config_entries/subentries/flow`. The websocket API only exposes
149	`subentries/list`, `subentries/update`, `subentries/delete` — no flow driving.
150	
151	That matters: a card **cannot** drive a subentry flow itself without rendering the
152	forms, which is the thing we are trying to escape. So the bonus depends entirely on
153	opening Home Assistant's *own* dialog.
154	
155	### Options, honestly ranked
156	
157	1. **Fire `show-dialog`.** The frontend's dialog manager listens for a `show-dialog`
158	   event carrying `dialogTag` / `dialogImport` / `dialogParams`. `dialogImport` is a
159	   function returning a dynamic import of a frontend-internal module, which a custom
160	   card has no import path for. It *may* work with `dialogTag` alone when the element
161	   is already defined — but that depends on whether the user has visited a page that
162	   loaded it, which is not a contract.
163	   **Status: unverified. Prototype before promising.** This is exactly the shape of
164	   claim `feedback_read_the_framework_before_claiming_a_limit` says to test rather

54	- Migration writes subentries from `users` + `slot_assignment` and stops there.
55	- The slot number stays the durable key, which is what
56	  `project_slot_number_is_two_keys_fused` concluded was correct: the key denotes a
57	  credential position, and reuse is right.
58	
59	### Option B — move identifiers onto `subentry_id`
60	
61	`subentry_id` is a ULID, never reused, immune to renames *and* to renumbering.
62	
63	- Fixes the "entity IDs derive from a mutable name" problem at the root.
64	- **But it renames every entity in every installation.** 5.0 already did that once
65	  (`project_lcm_5_0_0_released`, the rename notification, the recorder rules in
66	  `project_ha_recorder_rename_semantics`). Doing it again buys durability nobody
67	  has asked for.
68	- It also contradicts the settled position that the slot number *is* the identity
69	  of a credential position.
70	
71	**Recommendation: Option A.** Take the storage and UI benefits; leave identifiers
72	alone. Revisit B only if renaming becomes a real reported problem.
73	
74	## Shape
75	
76	`subentry_type` is **`"user"`**, not `"slot"` and not `"member"`. A subentry holds a
77	*person* — their name, credential, enabled state and condition. "Member" is the
78	other axis entirely: `EntryConfig.member()` took a **lock's** registry entry, and a
79	member is "an entity this entry keeps credentials on", which is what #1480's
80	`CONF_LOCKS` → `CONF_MEMBERS` rename is about. Users and members are the two sides
81	of the entry, and a subentry is a user.
82	
83	`"user"` also matches the vocabulary already in the service surface — `add_user`,
84	`delete_user`, `enable_user`, `disable_user` — so nothing has to be learned twice.
85	
86	```python
87	ConfigSubentry(
88	    subentry_type="user",
89	    title="Sarah Chen",          # the user's name; what the UI lists
90	    unique_id=str(slot_num),     # unique within the entry
91	    data={
92	        "slot": 3,               # the credential position
93	        "pin": "1234",
94	        "enabled": True,
95	        "condition": "calendar.bookings",   # optional
96	    },
97	)
98	```
99	
100	`EntryConfig` keeps its current external surface — `users`, `assignment`,
101	`name_for`, `slot`, `has_slot` — and reads from `entry.subentries` instead of
102	`entry.data`. Every caller above the config layer is unaffected. That is the whole
103	point of `EntryConfig` existing.
104	
105	`locks` and `availability_entities` stay on the entry: they belong to the entry,
106	not to any one user.
107	
108	## Keeping the services working
109	
110	Requirement, not a nice-to-have.
111	
112	| Action | After |
113	|---|---|
114	| `add_user` | allocate a slot as today, then `async_add_subentry(...)` |
115	| `delete_user` | `async_remove_subentry(entry, subentry_id)` |
116	| `set_credential` / `clear_credential` | `async_update_subentry(...)` with new `data` |
117	| `enable_user` / `disable_user` | same |
118	| `set_condition` / `clear_condition` | same |
119	
120	The name-addressed resolution added in 5.4.0 (`_stored_user`, `_slot_for_user`)
121	becomes a lookup over `entry.subentries.values()` matching `identity(title)`. One
122	helper changes; the six actions above do not.
123	
124	**Trap:** `async_update_subentry` replaces `data` wholesale. `SlotEntityCoordinator`
125	already learned this lesson for entry data — `_write_config_fields` coalesces
126	writes because "the update listener has not yet refreshed `runtime_data.config`
127	between two consecutive writes, leading the second write to drop the first". The
128	same coalescing has to survive the move, or `set_credential` immediately followed
129	by `enable_user` will drop the PIN.
130	
131	## The UI, and the bonus
132	
133	### What exists today
134	
135	`add-user-card.ts` hand-builds a form and calls `lock_code_manager.add_user`. It
136	hand-builds it because **custom cards cannot use Home Assistant's `ha-*` form
137	components** — they are not registered for custom elements, and an unregistered
138	`ha-*` renders as nothing at all, invisibly, with no DOM test able to catch it
139	(`feedback_dashboard_cards_cannot_use_ha_form_components`; it shipped twice).
140	
141	So the bonus is worth real points: if the card can hand the user to Home
142	Assistant's own subentry dialog, **Home Assistant renders the form** and the whole
143	class of bug disappears, along with the hand-built card.
144	
145	### What I verified
146	
147	Subentry flows are driven over **REST**, not websocket:
148	`/api/config/config_entries/subentries/flow`. The websocket API only exposes
149	`subentries/list`, `subentries/update`, `subentries/delete` — no flow driving.
150	
151	That matters: a card **cannot** drive a subentry flow itself without rendering the
152	forms, which is the thing we are trying to escape. So the bonus depends entirely on
153	opening Home Assistant's *own* dialog.
154	
155	### Options, honestly ranked
156	
157	1. **Fire `show-dialog`.** The frontend's dialog manager listens for a `show-dialog`
158	   event carrying `dialogTag` / `dialogImport` / `dialogParams`. `dialogImport` is a
159	   function returning a dynamic import of a frontend-internal module, which a custom
160	   card has no import path for. It *may* work with `dialogTag` alone when the element
161	   is already defined — but that depends on whether the user has visited a page that
162	   loaded it, which is not a contract.
163	   **Status: unverified. Prototype before promising.** This is exactly the shape of
164	   claim `feedback_read_the_framework_before_claiming_a_limit` says to test rather
