content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

content.description: Constants + async_validate_credential + ValidationResult + unit tests, TDD. Precedence: most restrictive wins (user_disabled > condition_not_met).

content.description: Add credential_used.yaml to the automation-blueprint list; add a feature bullet for validating codes entered outside LCM-managed locks. Direction/roadmap stays out.

content.description: Currently documents validate_code as a pure query with no events. Needs use_credential (source/target required), the unified event, and the new blueprint. Staged unpushed until merge.

content.description: docs/2026-08-25-session-handoff-1414.md describes the design as of stages 1-5 planned; update to what actually shipped.

content.description: #1485, #1486, #1487 — read each description against its actual final diff, not against the agent's report. #1487 especially: title and body predate the operation field, credential-type event_types, and the limiter input.

content.subject: Run code review on #1489 after fixes land
content.description: Fix agent a55956239d83904a5 is applying the three Important findings (declaration exit, orphan pruning, misleading copy) plus the registryless-entity minor. Run /code-review on 1489 once it commits and pushes.

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

Raman (maintainer of `lock_code_manager`, a Home Assistant custom integration) drove a long multi-PR arc. In this segment his explicit requests were, in order:

- Investigate what tracking non-provider members/locks still buys, given the event entity no longer needs the lock collection.
- Ship lock-less entries (the guard) plus an optional availability-source field — then, after seeing it, **remove the availability-source feature entirely**, keeping only the guard.
- Close #1494 and revert #1492, forcing entry-title identification for `use_credential`.
- Fix #1491 (reauth orphans a credential store) **straight to main**.
- Fix #1488 (credential-use visibility + limiter miscount).
- Remove the now-dead `CONF_MEMBERS` shape; check for other dead code via a feature-branch-vs-main diff.
- Clean up worktrees and stale branches; later, delete the two `/private/tmp` worktrees and `fix/config-flow-field-labels`.
- Update the wiki for ESPHome/external keypads/Virtual; verify Home and Sidebar; verify all services documented with accurate schemas; document the flat single-user shorthand.
- Create two PRs onto a new `v6` branch: (1) remove deprecated `set/clear_usercode` and `set/clear_slot_condition`; (2) switch to subentries for every slot. Then a third PR removing the deprecated event and related constants ("Don't forget to remove constants for services removed too").
- Mid-stream: "lets remove the old websocket commands and add new ones that mirror the services."
- Write up the subentry design; corrected `subentry_type` should be `"user"`; walk through the open questions; make `add_user`/`delete_user` accept lists with a coercion; add a normalizer to move flat keys under `users`.
- "keep going" on the remaining subentry test failures.

Standing constraints: don't merge without explicit say-so; keep PR descriptions readable/brief; use `.github/` templates; `prek` not `pre-commit`; run the full suite before pushing; design specs stay local-only in gitignored `docs/`.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
- HA config entries, options flows, reauth flows, update listeners, `async_update_entry`, `async_reload`
- **HA config subentries**: `ConfigSubentry(data, subentry_id, subentry_type, title, unique_id)`, `async_add_subentry` / `async_update_subentry` / `async_remove_subentry`, `ConfigSubentryFlow`, `async_get_supported_subentry_types`, `config_subentry_id` on entities and devices, `MockConfigEntry(subentries_data=...)`
- `EntityRegistryItems` indexes on `config_entry_id` alone (independent of `config_subentry_id`)
- Subentry flows are driven over **REST** (`/api/config/config_entries/subentries/flow`), not websocket
- `ObjectSelector` with `fields`, `multiple`, `label_field`, `description_field`
- `cv.ensure_list` (wraps non-list) vs `vol.Coerce(list)` (returns dict **keys** — a silent trap)
- LCM domain: `EntryConfig`, `SlotAssignment`, `SlotEntityCoordinator`, `BaseLock`, `CredentialType`, `MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES`, `identity()`/`normalize_name()`
- Mutation testing as the primary quality gate (100% line coverage repeatedly proved insufficient)
- Squash-merge semantics (merged branches never become ancestors)

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

- **`custom_components/lock_code_manager/entity.py`** — the entire lock-less feature, 5 lines:
```python
@callback
def _is_available(self) -> bool:
    """Return whether entity should be available."""
    if not self.locks:
        # Nothing to follow is not the same as nothing being up. An entry
        # with no locks answers for its credentials out of its own
        # configuration, which is present whenever the entry is loaded.
        return True
    return any(
        state.state != STATE_UNAVAILABLE
        for lock in self.locks
        if (state := self.hass.states.get(lock.lock.entity_id))
    )
```

- **`custom_components/lock_code_manager/domain/config.py`** — `from_entry` now reads subentries; `to_dict()` returns entry-only data; new `subentry_data(name)`; new `async_write_entry_config` (the single write path, matching users by `identity()`).

- **`custom_components/lock_code_manager/__init__.py`** — v4→v5 migration creating subentries and clearing `_MOVED_KEYS = frozenset({CONF_USERS, CONF_SLOTS, CONF_SLOT_ASSIGNMENT})` in the same write; listener reworked to diff cached-vs-current with `if not diff.has_changes: return`; setup calls `_async_apply_entry_update(hass, config_entry, EntryConfig.empty())`; rename helpers take `config: EntryConfig` explicitly.

- **`custom_components/lock_code_manager/domain/services.py`** — `async_add_users` / `async_delete_users` (batch, all-or-nothing, one allocation `len(config.users) + len(additions)`, one write); `_stored_user`, `_slot_for_user`, `_slot_coordinator_for`, `_managed_credential_type`; `_async_write_and_settle` now takes an `EntryConfig`.

- **`custom_components/lock_code_manager/domain/slot_coordinator.py`** — `_write_config_fields` routed through `async_write_entry_config` (was silently dropping every name/PIN/enabled change).

Corrected publicly; updated `feedback_git_commands_need_state_established_first` memory with the rule "before measuring or branching from a branch, compare it to its remote."
- **Heuristic test deletion**: swallowed a block of module-level constants (`VALIDATE_LOCK_ENTITY_ID` etc.) and left two `@pytest.mark.parametrize` decorators orphaned onto unrelated tests. Restored the file from HEAD and redid using AST spans (`node.lineno` + `decorator_list`).

- **Setup produced no entities**: listener diffed cached-vs-current, but setup had already cached the current config → no diff. Fixed by passing `EntryConfig.empty()` at setup.
- **v3→v4 rename helpers broke**: they called `EntryConfig.from_entry`, which mid-migration reads subentries that don't exist yet → entity IDs fell back to `code_slot_1`. Fixed by passing the migrated config explicitly.
- **Import placement**: inserts landed inside multi-line import blocks (SyntaxError) and used wrong relative depth (`..common` vs `...common`). Fixed via AST `end_lineno` placement.
- **Mutation survivors that found real gaps**: (a) `set_condition` skipping condition-entity validation was untested — added test; (b) allocating `len(users) + 1` instead of `+ len(batch)` broke nothing because fixtures had spare slots — added a test pinning the size allocation is asked for.

Solved: lock-less entries (5 lines vs #1489's ~1,150); reauth orphaning a cleartext-PIN store; credential-use invisibility while locks are down; limiter decrementing on recovery/restart; dead `CONF_MEMBERS` removal (+3/−525); four deprecated services and the deprecated event removed on v6; list-taking user services with full backward compatibility; wiki accuracy verified programmatically against shipped `services.yaml` (16/16 match).

Design doc: `docs/2026-08-27-subentries-design.md` (local only). Tracking issue #1481.
Branch `feat/users-as-subentries` off `v6`, worktree `.worktrees/subentries`.
WIP commit `7bf6ae7b`. **154 tests failing, 2126 passing** — down from 389.

## Settled decisions

- **`subentry_type = "user"`**, not `"slot"` or `"member"`. A member is the *lock*
  side (`EntryConfig.member()` took a lock's registry entry); a user is the person.
- **Option A on identifiers**: slot number stays in unique IDs, so nothing renames.
  5.0 already renamed everything once; doing it again buys durability nobody asked for.
- **Users move to subentries; the options flow keeps locks only.** Not keeping the
  YAML users field alongside — two write paths to one dataset is the recurring failure.
- Bulk editing was the only real cost, and the list-taking `add_user` (#1509, shipped
  in 5.5.0) replaces it with a typed repeatable form.

## Built and verified

- `EntryConfig.from_entry` reads `entry.subentries`; each user's slot lives in their
  own subentry, so **`slot_assignment` is gone** — the two can no longer disagree.
- `async_write_entry_config` — the single write path, matching users **by identity**
  so a rename updates the person rather than delete-plus-add.
- `to_dict()` now returns the *entry's* data only; `subentry_data(name)` returns one
  user's.
- Migration v4→v5 creates subentries and clears the old keys in the same write that
  bumps the version. `ConfigFlow.VERSION = 5` — bumping the data without the
  declaration gives `MIGRATION_ERROR` on an entry "newer than supported".
- Verified end to end: entry migrates, loads, `name_for(1)` resolves.

## The listener rework this forced

`_async_apply_entry_update` used to diff `data` (old) against `options` (new) and
early-return on `if not config_entry.options`. That is the options-flow convention:
the flow stages changes in options, the listener diffs and then settles them back.

Users in subentries never touch options, so entities were never created. Subentry
writes *do* notify update listeners (verified in HA source) — the gate was the
problem, not the notification.

Now: capture `runtime_data.config` **before** refreshing it, diff cached-vs-current,
and gate on `diff.has_changes`. That sees both halves and is its own recursion guard,
because the settle write produces no diff. Setup passes `EntryConfig.empty()` as the
old state — at setup everything is new, and diffing against the cache finds nothing.

## Remaining

Mostly tests asserting the old storage shape: `assert entry.version == 4`,
`entry.data["users"]` reads, and migration tests expecting particular entity IDs.
Fixtures themselves needed no changes — `MockConfigEntry` defaults to version 1, so
they flow through the whole migration chain.

Then: entity/device `config_subentry_id` binding (design step 4), the subentry flow
(step 1, deliberately after the model is real), and the frontend dialog prototype
(step 5, `feedback_dashboard_cards_cannot_use_ha_form_components` applies).

description: "Branch from an explicit base, verify that base is current, and never run a work-moving git command without first checking what state the tree is actually in"
metadata:

Four incidents, all the same disease — a git command run without establishing state first:

1. **`git checkout -b` from the wrong branch.** Created `feat/rename-notice-not-repair` while standing on `feat/user-centric-card` instead of `v3`. The PR carried five commits of unreviewed card work, and merging it put all of that into `v3` — described nowhere in its body.
2. **`git stash` on an already-clean tree.** It saved nothing, so the later `pop` applied an unrelated stash from three weeks earlier. See [[feedback_never_drop_a_stash_you_did_not_verify]].
3. **`git checkout -- <file>`** to strip a debug print, which discarded a new test and four fixes with it.
4. **Measured a diff against a stale local branch.** Local `feature/credential-store-model` was four merged PRs behind `origin/`. `git diff <stale-local>...HEAD` attributed #1485/#1486/#1487/#1492's changes to #1489, so I told Raman it was "+1,702 lines across 21 files" when it was +1,146 across 13 — a ~33% overstatement, quoted while recommending he abandon it. A worktree cut from that same stale tip then made `git revert` of an absent commit produce phantom conflicts referencing symbols that didn't exist on the branch.

**Why:** each felt routine, so none got a state check first. The cost isn't the mistake, it's that most were silent — a merge that ships unmentioned code, a stash pop that succeeds, and a diff stat that prints a confident wrong number all look exactly like success.

**How to apply:**

- Always `git checkout -b <new> <base>`. The bare form silently inherits whatever is checked out.
- **Before measuring or branching from a branch, compare it to its remote.** `git rev-parse <branch> origin/<branch>` — if they differ, you are about to quote or build on the wrong tree. Prefer `origin/<branch>` as the explicit base.
- A number that feeds a recommendation gets the same verification as a code change. See [[feedback_no_unsourced_claims]].
- Phantom merge/revert conflicts naming symbols that don't exist on the branch mean the base is wrong, not that the conflict is subtle. Stop and check the history before resolving.
- Before opening a PR, run `git log --oneline <base>..HEAD`. If the commit list is longer than the story the PR tells, the branch point was wrong.
- Never reach for `stash` or `checkout --` to "be safe". Check `git status` first.
- Working directory can drift back to the primary checkout between Bash calls. Use `git -C <abs-path>` when a worktree is in play — see [[feedback_absolute_paths_when_worktree_exists]].

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The distinguishing factor isn't "does the fixture use `CONF_SLOTS`" — it's **does the entry ever get set up**. Entries that go through `async_setup_entry` hit the v4→v5 migration and grow their subentries for free; fixtures that only `add_to_hass()` and then construct a provider object directly never migrate, so they must supply `subentries_data` themselves. That's why the bulk grep over-reported.

Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

import ast
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def slots_key(node):
    """Return the index of the CONF_SLOTS key in a Dict node, or None."""
    for i, k in enumerate(node.keys):
        if isinstance(k, ast.Name) and k.id == "CONF_SLOTS":
            return i
    return None


def rewrite(path: Path, only_lines: set[int] | None) -> int:
    src = path.read_text()
    tree = ast.parse(src)
    edits = []
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if not (
            isinstance(node, ast.Call)
            and isinstance(node.func, ast.Name)
            and node.func.id == "MockConfigEntry"
        ):
            continue
        if only_lines is not None and node.lineno not in only_lines:
            continue
        if any(kw.arg in ("subentries_data", "version") for kw in node.keywords):
            continue
        data_kw = next((kw for kw in node.keywords if kw.arg == "data"), None)
        if data_kw is None or not isinstance(data_kw.value, ast.Dict):
            continue
        d = data_kw.value
        idx = slots_key(d)
        if idx is None:
            continue
        slots_src = ast.get_source_segment(src, d.values[idx])
        others = [
            f"{ast.get_source_segment(src, k)}: {ast.get_source_segment(src, v)}"
            for i, (k, v) in enumerate(zip(d.keys, d.values))
            if i != idx
        ]
        # Indent the inserted keyword to match the `data=` keyword's own line.
        lines = src.splitlines(keepends=True)
        offsets = [0]
        for line in lines:
            offsets.append(offsets[-1] + len(line))
        line_text = lines[d.lineno - 1]
        indent = " " * (len(line_text) - len(line_text.lstrip()))
        start = offsets[d.lineno - 1] + d.col_offset
        end = offsets[d.end_lineno - 1] + d.end_col_offset
        new = (
            "{" + ", ".join(others) + "},\n"
            + indent + f"subentries_data=user_subentries({slots_src})"
        )
        edits.append((start, end, new))

    for start, end, new in sorted(edits, reverse=True):
        src = src[:start] + new + src[end:]
    if edits:
        path.write_text(src)
    return len(edits)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    target = Path(sys.argv[1])
    lines = {int(x) for x in sys.argv[2:]} or None
    print(rewrite(target, lines), "rewritten in", target)

content.subject: Task 1: Validation core (domain/validation.py)
content.description: Constants + async_validate_credential + ValidationResult + unit tests, TDD. Precedence: most restrictive wins (user_disabled > condition_not_met).

content.subject: Task 2: ReaderLock provider + dispatch
content.description: providers/reader.py subclassing VirtualLock, non-lock-domain dispatch in resolve_provider_class_for_entity, state listener, tests.

content.subject: Task 3: Config flow readers selector
content.description: Optional readers field (sensor/text) on user + options steps, merge into CONF_LOCKS, at_least_one error, strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 4: validate_code service
content.description: Service registration with SupportsResponse.OPTIONAL, multi-entry handling, services.yaml + strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 5: Property test validation ⇔ active sensor
content.description: Hypothesis property test in tests/properties/ asserting validation agrees with active binary sensor.

content.subject: Task 6: Reader E2E + full suite verification
content.description: Full-stack reader E2E incl. mixed entry, websocket/strategy tolerance check, full pytest + prek, 100% coverage.

content.subject: Task 7: Wiki page + issue comment (post-merge)
content.description: Keypad/PIN-only wiki page (no RFID yet, decided 2026-08-25) and #1414 comment describing both options.

content.subject: Fix final-review criticals and importants
content.description: Critical 1 shared-instance multi-entry; Critical 2 ATTR_STATE cleartext; Imp 3 stale revalidation; Imp 4 diagnostics; Imp 5 normalization; Minor precedence duplication.

content.subject: Update PR #1475 title and description
content.description: Retitle for use_credential + unified event + blueprint; rewrite body (currently describes validate_code as a pure query, which is two designs stale).

content.subject: Update README for shipped items
content.description: Add credential_used.yaml to the automation-blueprint list; add a feature bullet for validating codes entered outside LCM-managed locks. Direction/roadmap stays out.

content.subject: Rewrite wiki External-Keypads page
content.description: Currently documents validate_code as a pure query with no events. Needs use_credential (source/target required), the unified event, and the new blueprint. Staged unpushed until merge.

content.subject: Refresh session handoff doc
content.description: docs/2026-08-25-session-handoff-1414.md describes the design as of stages 1-5 planned; update to what actually shipped.

content.subject: Verify all three PR titles and descriptions before handoff
content.description: #1485, #1486, #1487 — read each description against its actual final diff, not against the agent's report. #1487 especially: title and body predate the operation field, credential-type event_types, and the limiter input.

content.subject: Run code review on #1489 after fixes land
content.description: Fix agent a55956239d83904a5 is applying the three Important findings (declaration exit, orphan pruning, misleading copy) plus the registryless-entity minor. Run /code-review on 1489 once it commits and pushes.

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

content.subject: Task 1: Validation core (domain/validation.py)
content.description: Constants + async_validate_credential + ValidationResult + unit tests, TDD. Precedence: most restrictive wins (user_disabled > condition_not_met).

content.description: Retitle for use_credential + unified event + blueprint; rewrite body (currently describes validate_code as a pure query, which is two designs stale).

content.subject: Update README for shipped items
content.description: Add credential_used.yaml to the automation-blueprint list; add a feature bullet for validating codes entered outside LCM-managed locks. Direction/roadmap stays out.

content.subject: Rewrite wiki External-Keypads page
content.description: Currently documents validate_code as a pure query with no events. Needs use_credential (source/target required), the unified event, and the new blueprint. Staged unpushed until merge.

content.subject: Refresh session handoff doc
content.description: docs/2026-08-25-session-handoff-1414.md describes the design as of stages 1-5 planned; update to what actually shipped.

content.subject: Verify all three PR titles and descriptions before handoff
content.description: #1485, #1486, #1487 — read each description against its actual final diff, not against the agent's report. #1487 especially: title and body predate the operation field, credential-type event_types, and the limiter input.

content.subject: Run code review on #1489 after fixes land
content.description: Fix agent a55956239d83904a5 is applying the three Important findings (declaration exit, orphan pruning, misleading copy) plus the registryless-entity minor. Run /code-review on 1489 once it commits and pushes.

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

content.subject: Task 1: Validation core (domain/validation.py)
content.description: Constants + async_validate_credential + ValidationResult + unit tests, TDD. Precedence: most restrictive wins (user_disabled > condition_not_met).

content.subject: Task 2: ReaderLock provider + dispatch
content.description: providers/reader.py subclassing VirtualLock, non-lock-domain dispatch in resolve_provider_class_for_entity, state listener, tests.

content.subject: Task 3: Config flow readers selector
content.description: Optional readers field (sensor/text) on user + options steps, merge into CONF_LOCKS, at_least_one error, strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 4: validate_code service
content.description: Service registration with SupportsResponse.OPTIONAL, multi-entry handling, services.yaml + strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 5: Property test validation ⇔ active sensor
content.description: Hypothesis property test in tests/properties/ asserting validation agrees with active binary sensor.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)

UNMANAGED_ISSUE_KEY = "unmanaged_code"


def unmanaged_issue_id(lock_entity_id: str, slot: int) -> str:
    """Build the repair issue id for one unmanaged code."""
    return f"{UNMANAGED_ISSUE_KEY}_{lock_entity_id}_{slot}"


async def async_sweep_unmanaged_codes(
    hass: HomeAssistant, config_entry: ConfigEntry
) -> None:
    """
    Raise a repair for each code on this entry's locks that nothing manages.

    Runs from the migration, so it builds throwaway providers rather than
    using the entry's own: setup has not happened yet. A lock that cannot
    be read is skipped with a warning rather than failing the migration --
    the entry has to load, and a sleeping battery lock must not stop it.
    That lock's codes go unreported, which is the accepted cost of doing
    this exactly once.
    """
    dev_reg = dr.async_get(hass)
    ent_reg = er.async_get(hass)
    locks = config_entry.options.get(CONF_LOCKS, config_entry.data.get(CONF_LOCKS, []))

    for lock_entity_id in locks:
        # Building the provider is itself allowed to fail (a lock entity that
        # has gone away), and failing there means there is nothing to release:
        # the borrowed-instance block is never entered.
        try:
            async with borrowed_lock_instance(
                async_create_lock_instance(
                    hass, dev_reg, ent_reg, config_entry, lock_entity_id
                )
            ) as lock:
                credentials = await lock.async_get_usercodes()
        except Exception:
            _LOGGER.warning(
                "Could not read %s while checking for codes this integration does "
                "not manage; any it holds will not be reported",
                lock_entity_id,
                exc_info=True,
            )
            continue

        # Across every entry, not just this one: two entries sharing a lock
        # would otherwise each report the other's codes.
        managed = get_managed_slots(hass, lock_entity_id)
        unmanaged = sorted(
            slot
            for slot, credential in credentials.items()
            if slot not in managed and credential.is_present
        )
        if not unmanaged:
            continue

        _LOGGER.info(
            "Lock %s holds %s code(s) no configuration accounts for, in slot(s) %s; "
            "raising a repair for each",
            lock_entity_id,
            len(unmanaged),
            ", ".join(str(slot) for slot in unmanaged),
        )
        for slot in unmanaged:
            ir.async_create_issue(
                hass,
                DOMAIN,
                unmanaged_issue_id(lock_entity_id, slot),
                is_fixable=True,

content.text:
`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
This is a **real migration-ordering bug**, not a test artifact. `async_sweep_unmanaged_codes` runs inside the v3→v4 step and calls `get_managed_slots`, which reads `EntryConfig.from_entry` — which now reads *subentries*. Mid-chain the entry hasn't reached v5 yet, so its users are still in `data[CONF_SLOTS]` and its subentries are empty. The sweep therefore sees zero managed slots and raises a repair for every one of the entry's **own** codes. Anyone upgrading from v3 gets a wall of bogus repairs.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

content.description: Constants + async_validate_credential + ValidationResult + unit tests, TDD. Precedence: most restrictive wins (user_disabled > condition_not_met).

content.subject: Task 2: ReaderLock provider + dispatch
content.description: providers/reader.py subclassing VirtualLock, non-lock-domain dispatch in resolve_provider_class_for_entity, state listener, tests.

content.subject: Task 3: Config flow readers selector
content.description: Optional readers field (sensor/text) on user + options steps, merge into CONF_LOCKS, at_least_one error, strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 4: validate_code service
content.description: Service registration with SupportsResponse.OPTIONAL, multi-entry handling, services.yaml + strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 5: Property test validation ⇔ active sensor
content.description: Hypothesis property test in tests/properties/ asserting validation agrees with active binary sensor.

content.subject: Task 6: Reader E2E + full suite verification
content.description: Full-stack reader E2E incl. mixed entry, websocket/strategy tolerance check, full pytest + prek, 100% coverage.

content.subject: Task 7: Wiki page + issue comment (post-merge)
content.description: Keypad/PIN-only wiki page (no RFID yet, decided 2026-08-25) and #1414 comment describing both options.

content.subject: Fix final-review criticals and importants

content.subject: Update PR #1475 title and description
content.description: Retitle for use_credential + unified event + blueprint; rewrite body (currently describes validate_code as a pure query, which is two designs stale).

content.subject: Rewrite wiki External-Keypads page
content.description: Currently documents validate_code as a pure query with no events. Needs use_credential (source/target required), the unified event, and the new blueprint. Staged unpushed until merge.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

class LockCodeManagerOptionsFlow(config_entries.OptionsFlow):
    """Options flow for Lock Code Manager."""

    async def async_step_init(
        self, user_input: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Edit the entry's users. Numbers are not part of this."""
        errors: dict[str, str] = {}
        description_placeholders: dict[str, Any] = {}
        if not user_input:
            user_input = {}

        if user_input:
            # Accumulated alongside the users validation rather than
            # short-circuiting it: both refusals render together, so one round
            # trip shows everything wrong with the submission.
            lock_errors, lock_placeholders = _check_unclaimed_mqtt_locks(
                self.hass,
                user_input[CONF_LOCKS],
                get_entry_config(self.config_entry).locks,
            )
            errors.update(lock_errors)
            description_placeholders.update(lock_placeholders)

            (
                users,
                validation_errors,
                validation_placeholders,
            ) = await _async_validate_users_yaml(
                self.hass,
                self.config_entry,
                user_input[CONF_USERS],
                user_input[CONF_LOCKS],
            )
            errors.update(validation_errors)
            description_placeholders.update(validation_placeholders)

            if not errors:
                assert users is not None
                (
                    unavailable,
                    allocation_errors,
                    allocation_placeholders,
                ) = await _allocate_for(
                    self.hass,
                    self.config_entry,
                    user_input[CONF_LOCKS],
                    len(users),
                )
                if unavailable is None:
                    errors.update(allocation_errors)
                    description_placeholders.update(allocation_placeholders)
                else:
                    config = get_entry_config(self.config_entry)
                    # Reconciled against what the entry already holds, so a
                    # user who was here before keeps their number and only
                    # newcomers are issued one. Moving somebody would rewrite
                    # their credential on every lock.
                    assignment = config.assignment.reconcile(
                        users, start=1, unavailable=unavailable
                    )
                    # Written through EntryConfig so whatever else the entry
                    # carries survives the edit. Building the dict by hand
                    # drops every key this form does not ask about.
                    return self.async_create_entry(
                        title="",
                        data=EntryConfig(
                            locks=tuple(user_input[CONF_LOCKS]),
                            users=users,
                            assignment=assignment,
                            extra=config.extra,
                        ).to_dict(),
                    )

        config = get_entry_config(self.config_entry)
        # Plain dict/list, because the form selectors cannot serialize the
        # deeply read-only mappings EntryConfig uses internally.
        defaults = {
            CONF_LOCKS: list(config.locks),
            CONF_USERS: {name: dict(user) for name, user in config.users.items()},
        }

        return self.async_show_form(
            step_id="init",
            data_schema=vol.Schema(
                {
                    vol.Required(
                        CONF_LOCKS,
                        default=user_input.get(CONF_LOCKS, defaults[CONF_LOCKS]),
                    ): LOCK_ENTITY_SELECTOR,
                    vol.Required(
                        CONF_USERS,
                        default=user_input.get(CONF_USERS, defaults[CONF_USERS]),
                    ): SLOTS_YAML_SELECTOR,
                }
            ),
            errors=errors,
            description_placeholders=description_placeholders,
            last_step=True,
        )

async def _async_apply_entry_update(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    config_entry: LockCodeManagerConfigEntry,
    old_config: EntryConfig | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Bring entities, devices and locks into line with the entry."""
    # Refresh the cached EntryConfig on EVERY update — including entity-driven
    # writes that go straight to data with empty options (e.g. a slot's name or
    # PIN being edited via its text entity). The early-return below skips the
    # entity-creation pass for those cases, but downstream readers via
    # runtime_data.config still need to see the current data.
    runtime_data = config_entry.runtime_data
    # What the entry looked like when this pass started, captured before the
    # refresh below overwrites it. Users live in subentries and locks may be
    # on either side, so comparing the cached view against the current one
    # is the only comparison that sees both.
    # ``None`` means "compare against what we last saw". Setup passes an empty
    # config instead, because at that point nothing has been created yet and
    # every user is new -- diffing against the cache would find no changes and

def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Return the ENTRY's own data, suitable for ``async_update_entry``.

        Users are not in here: they live in subentries, and
        :func:`async_write_entry_config` is what puts them there. This carries
        only what belongs to the entry itself, so a caller cannot write a user
        into entry data by accident and give the entry two answers about who
        holds a slot.
        """
        return {
            **dict(self.extra),
            CONF_LOCKS: list(self.locks),
        }

    def subentry_data(self, name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return the subentry ``data`` for one user, number included."""
        data = dict(self.users[name])
        if (slot_num := self.assignment.slot(name)) is not None:
            data[CONF_SLOT] = slot_num
        return data

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

):
    """Base class for config subentry flows."""

    _flow_result = SubentryFlowResult
    handler: tuple[str, str]

    @callback
    @override
    def async_create_entry(
        self,
        *,
        title: str | None = None,
        data: Mapping[str, Any],
        description: str | None = None,
        description_placeholders: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
        unique_id: str | None = None,
    ) -> SubentryFlowResult:
        """Finish config flow and create a config entry."""
        if self.source != SOURCE_USER:
            raise ValueError(f"Source is {self.source}, expected {SOURCE_USER}")

        result = super().async_create_entry(
            title=title,
            data=data,
            description=description,
            description_placeholders=description_placeholders,
        )

        result["unique_id"] = unique_id

        return result

    @callback
    def _async_update(
        self,
        entry: ConfigEntry,
        subentry: ConfigSubentry,
        *,
        unique_id: str | UndefinedType | None = UNDEFINED,
        title: str | UndefinedType = UNDEFINED,
        data: Mapping[str, Any] | UndefinedType = UNDEFINED,
        data_updates: Mapping[str, Any] | UndefinedType = UNDEFINED,
    ) -> bool:
        """Update config subentry and return result.

        Internal to be used by update_and_abort and
        update_reload_and_abort methods only.
        """

        if data_updates is not UNDEFINED:
            if data is not UNDEFINED:
                raise ValueError("Cannot set both data and data_updates")
            data = subentry.data | data_updates
        return self.hass.config_entries.async_update_subentry(
            entry=entry,
            subentry=subentry,
            unique_id=unique_id,
            title=title,
            data=data,
        )

    @callback
    def async_update_and_abort(
        self,
        entry: ConfigEntry,
        subentry: ConfigSubentry,
        *,
        unique_id: str | UndefinedType | None = UNDEFINED,
        title: str | UndefinedType = UNDEFINED,
        data: Mapping[str, Any] | UndefinedType = UNDEFINED,
        data_updates: Mapping[str, Any] | UndefinedType = UNDEFINED,
    ) -> SubentryFlowResult:
        """Update config subentry and finish subentry flow.

        :param data: replace the subentry data with new data
        :param data_updates: add items from data_updates to subentry data - existing
        keys are overridden
        :param title: replace the title of the subentry
        :param unique_id: replace the unique_id of the subentry
        """
        self._async_update(
            entry=entry,
            subentry=subentry,
            unique_id=unique_id,
            title=title,
            data=data,
            data_updates=data_updates,
        )
        return self.async_abort(reason="reconfigure_successful")

    @callback
    def async_update_reload_and_abort(
        self,
        entry: ConfigEntry,
        subentry: ConfigSubentry,
        *,
        unique_id: str | UndefinedType | None = UNDEFINED,
        title: str | UndefinedType = UNDEFINED,
        data: Mapping[str, Any] | UndefinedType = UNDEFINED,
        data_updates: Mapping[str, Any] | UndefinedType = UNDEFINED,
        reload_even_if_entry_is_unchanged: bool = True,
    ) -> SubentryFlowResult:
        """Update config subentry, reload config entry and finish subentry flow.

        :param data: replace the subentry data with new data
        :param data_updates: add items from data_updates to subentry data - existing
        keys are overridden
        :param title: replace the title of the subentry
        :param unique_id: replace the unique_id of the subentry
        :param reload_even_if_entry_is_unchanged: set this to `False` if the entry
        should not be reloaded if it is unchanged
        """
        result = self._async_update(
            entry=entry,
            subentry=subentry,
            unique_id=unique_id,
            title=title,
            data=data,
            data_updates=data_updates,
        )
        if reload_even_if_entry_is_unchanged or result:
            if entry.update_listeners:
                raise ValueError("Cannot update and reload entry with update listeners")
            self.hass.config_entries.async_schedule_reload(entry.entry_id)
        return self.async_abort(reason="reconfigure_successful")
