content.description: Constants + async_validate_credential + ValidationResult + unit tests, TDD. Precedence: most restrictive wins (user_disabled > condition_not_met).

content.subject: Task 2: ReaderLock provider + dispatch
content.description: providers/reader.py subclassing VirtualLock, non-lock-domain dispatch in resolve_provider_class_for_entity, state listener, tests.

content.subject: Task 3: Config flow readers selector
content.description: Optional readers field (sensor/text) on user + options steps, merge into CONF_LOCKS, at_least_one error, strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 4: validate_code service
content.description: Service registration with SupportsResponse.OPTIONAL, multi-entry handling, services.yaml + strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 5: Property test validation ⇔ active sensor
content.description: Hypothesis property test in tests/properties/ asserting validation agrees with active binary sensor.

content.subject: Task 6: Reader E2E + full suite verification
content.description: Full-stack reader E2E incl. mixed entry, websocket/strategy tolerance check, full pytest + prek, 100% coverage.

content.subject: Task 7: Wiki page + issue comment (post-merge)
content.description: Keypad/PIN-only wiki page (no RFID yet, decided 2026-08-25) and #1414 comment describing both options.

content.subject: Fix final-review criticals and importants
content.description: Critical 1 shared-instance multi-entry; Critical 2 ATTR_STATE cleartext; Imp 3 stale revalidation; Imp 4 diagnostics; Imp 5 normalization; Minor precedence duplication.

content.subject: Update PR #1475 title and description
content.description: Retitle for use_credential + unified event + blueprint; rewrite body (currently describes validate_code as a pure query, which is two designs stale).

content.subject: Update README for shipped items
content.description: Add credential_used.yaml to the automation-blueprint list; add a feature bullet for validating codes entered outside LCM-managed locks. Direction/roadmap stays out.

content.subject: Rewrite wiki External-Keypads page
content.description: Currently documents validate_code as a pure query with no events. Needs use_credential (source/target required), the unified event, and the new blueprint. Staged unpushed until merge.

content.subject: Refresh session handoff doc
content.description: docs/2026-08-25-session-handoff-1414.md describes the design as of stages 1-5 planned; update to what actually shipped.

content.subject: Verify all three PR titles and descriptions before handoff
content.description: #1485, #1486, #1487 — read each description against its actual final diff, not against the agent's report. #1487 especially: title and body predate the operation field, credential-type event_types, and the limiter input.

content.subject: Run code review on #1489 after fixes land
content.description: Fix agent a55956239d83904a5 is applying the three Important findings (declaration exit, orphan pruning, misleading copy) plus the registryless-entity minor. Run /code-review on 1489 once it commits and pushes.

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

content.description: Service registration with SupportsResponse.OPTIONAL, multi-entry handling, services.yaml + strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 5: Property test validation ⇔ active sensor
content.description: Hypothesis property test in tests/properties/ asserting validation agrees with active binary sensor.

content.subject: Task 6: Reader E2E + full suite verification
content.description: Full-stack reader E2E incl. mixed entry, websocket/strategy tolerance check, full pytest + prek, 100% coverage.

content.subject: Task 7: Wiki page + issue comment (post-merge)
content.description: Keypad/PIN-only wiki page (no RFID yet, decided 2026-08-25) and #1414 comment describing both options.

content.subject: Fix final-review criticals and importants
content.description: Critical 1 shared-instance multi-entry; Critical 2 ATTR_STATE cleartext; Imp 3 stale revalidation; Imp 4 diagnostics; Imp 5 normalization; Minor precedence duplication.

content.subject: Update PR #1475 title and description
content.description: Retitle for use_credential + unified event + blueprint; rewrite body (currently describes validate_code as a pure query, which is two designs stale).

content.subject: Update README for shipped items
content.description: Add credential_used.yaml to the automation-blueprint list; add a feature bullet for validating codes entered outside LCM-managed locks. Direction/roadmap stays out.

content.subject: Rewrite wiki External-Keypads page
content.description: Currently documents validate_code as a pure query with no events. Needs use_credential (source/target required), the unified event, and the new blueprint. Staged unpushed until merge.

content.subject: Refresh session handoff doc
content.description: docs/2026-08-25-session-handoff-1414.md describes the design as of stages 1-5 planned; update to what actually shipped.

content.subject: Verify all three PR titles and descriptions before handoff
content.description: #1485, #1486, #1487 — read each description against its actual final diff, not against the agent's report. #1487 especially: title and body predate the operation field, credential-type event_types, and the limiter input.

content.subject: Run code review on #1489 after fixes land
content.description: Fix agent a55956239d83904a5 is applying the three Important findings (declaration exit, orphan pruning, misleading copy) plus the registryless-entity minor. Run /code-review on 1489 once it commits and pushes.

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

async def test_options_flow(hass: HomeAssistant, mock_lock_config_entry):
    """Test options flow."""
    entry = MockConfigEntry(domain=DOMAIN, data=BASE_CONFIG, unique_id="Mock Title")
    entry.add_to_hass(hass)
    # The options flow now rejects the deprecated number_of_uses key, so build
    # the user-submitted config from scratch without it. Real entries have it
    # auto-stripped during migration before any options-flow interaction.
    new_config = {
        CONF_LOCKS: list(BASE_CONFIG[CONF_LOCKS]),
        CONF_USERS: {
            "test1": {CONF_PIN: "1234", CONF_ENABLED: True},
            "test2": {
                CONF_PIN: "5678",
                CONF_ENABLED: True,
                CONF_CONDITION: "calendar.test_1",
            },
            "User 3": {CONF_ENABLED: True, CONF_PIN: ""},
        },
    }
    result = await hass.config_entries.options.async_init(entry.entry_id)

    assert result["type"] == "form"
    assert result["step_id"] == "init"
    flow_id = result["flow_id"]

    result = await hass.config_entries.options.async_configure(
        flow_id, user_input=new_config
    )

    assert result["type"] == "form"
    assert result["step_id"] == "init"
    assert result["errors"] == {"base": "invalid_config"}

    # Give the enabled user a PIN and it saves.
    new_config[CONF_USERS]["User 3"][CONF_PIN] = "1234"
    with _holding():
        result = await hass.config_entries.options.async_configure(
            flow_id, user_input=new_config
        )

    assert result["type"] == "create_entry"
    assert result["data"][CONF_USERS] == new_config[CONF_USERS]
    # Numbers are issued here, not submitted.
    assert set(result["data"][CONF_SLOT_ASSIGNMENT]) == {"test1", "test2", "user 3"}

async def test_config_flow_slots_already_configured(
    hass: HomeAssistant, mock_lock_config_entry, lock_code_manager_config_entry
):
    """Another entry's numbers are avoided, not reported as a conflict.

    Picking a number another entry manages used to be something the user
    could do and be told off for. Now allocation simply does not issue one.
    """
    flow_id = await _start_yaml_config_flow(hass)

    with _holding():
        result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
            flow_id,
            {CONF_USERS: {"User 2": {CONF_ENABLED: False, CONF_PIN: "0123"}}},
        )

    assert result["type"] == "create_entry"
    taken = set(get_entry_config(lock_code_manager_config_entry).slot_numbers)
    assert not set(result["data"][CONF_SLOT_ASSIGNMENT].values()) & taken

async def test_ui_setup_allocates_around_existing_codes(
    hass: HomeAssistant, mock_lock_config_entry
):
    """Setup skips slots that already hold a code instead of asking about them.

    There is no prompt because there is nothing to overwrite: the numbers are
    chosen, not requested, so an occupied one is simply not offered. The
    confirmation the flow used to show existed because the user picked a range
    and might have picked one already in use.
    """
    flow_id = await _init_flow_to_user_step(hass)
    await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
        flow_id, {CONF_NAME: "test", CONF_LOCKS: [LOCK_1_ENTITY_ID]}
    )
    await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(flow_id, {"next_step_id": "ui"})
    result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
        flow_id, {CONF_NUM_USERS: 2}

########## test_setup_reads_only_as_far_as_it_has_to  [1012-1058]
async def test_setup_reads_only_as_far_as_it_has_to(
    hass: HomeAssistant, mock_lock_config_entry
):
    """The window starts at the number of users and widens by what is in the way.

    Locks that answer one index per round trip make the width of this read
    its cost, so a lock is never walked to its advertised capacity to place a
    handful of users.
    """
    windows: list[list[int]] = []

    async def _read(self, slots=None):
        scope = sorted(self.managed_slots if slots is None else slots)
        windows.append(scope)
        return {
            slot: (
                SlotCredential.known("0000")
                if slot in (1, 2, 3)
                else SlotCredential.empty()
            )
            for slot in scope
        }

    flow_id = await _start_config_flow(hass)
    await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(flow_id, {"next_step_id": "ui"})

    with patch.object(MockLCMLock, "async_get_usercodes", _read):
        result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
            flow_id, {CONF_NUM_USERS: 2}
        )
        for name in ("Raman", "Alice"):
            result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
                flow_id, {CONF_NAME: name, CONF_ENABLED: True, CONF_PIN: "1111"}
            )

    assert result["type"] == "create_entry"
    # Slots 1-3 are taken, so the two users land on 4 and 5.
    assert result["data"][CONF_SLOT_ASSIGNMENT] == {"alice": 4, "raman": 5}
    # Every number issued was one that was actually read -- not merely one
    # below the highest read, which would let a gap through if the read ever
    # stops being contiguous.
    assert set(result["data"][CONF_SLOT_ASSIGNMENT].values()) <= {
        slot for window in windows for slot in window
    }
    # Asked about 1-2, then only 3-4, then only 5: every index once, and
    # never about the lock's whole capacity.
    assert windows == [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5]]

########## test_a_nearly_full_lock_is_read_once_through  [1598-1641]
async def test_a_nearly_full_lock_is_read_once_through(
    hass: HomeAssistant, mock_lock_config_entry
):
    """No index is asked about twice, however many passes it takes.

    Widening from the count re-reading everything each pass costs a lock
    holding codes low down several times its own capacity to place a couple
    of users -- on the providers that answer one index per round trip, that
    is the cost this whole approach exists to avoid.
    """
    asked: list[int] = []
    occupied = set(range(1, 30))

    async def _read(self, slots=None):
        scope = sorted(self.managed_slots if slots is None else slots)
        asked.extend(scope)
        return {
            slot: (
                SlotCredential.known("0000")
                if slot in occupied
                else SlotCredential.empty()
            )
            for slot in scope
        }

    flow_id = await _start_config_flow(hass)
    await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(flow_id, {"next_step_id": "ui"})

    with patch.object(MockLCMLock, "async_get_usercodes", _read):
        result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
            flow_id, {CONF_NUM_USERS: 2}
        )

    assert result["step_id"] == "code_slot"
    # The users land on 30 and 31, so 31 indices are read -- each exactly once.
    assert sorted(asked) == list(range(1, 32))
    assert len(asked) == len(set(asked)), "an index was read more than once"

    for name in ("Raman", "Alice"):
        result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
            flow_id, {CONF_NAME: name, CONF_ENABLED: True, CONF_PIN: "1111"}
        )
    assert result["type"] == "create_entry"
    assert set(result["data"][CONF_SLOT_ASSIGNMENT].values()) <= set(asked)

########## test_setup_reads_only_as_far_as_it_has_to  [1012-1058]
async def test_setup_reads_only_as_far_as_it_has_to(
    hass: HomeAssistant, mock_lock_config_entry
):
    """The window starts at the number of users and widens by what is in the way.

    Locks that answer one index per round trip make the width of this read
    its cost, so a lock is never walked to its advertised capacity to place a
    handful of users.
    """
    windows: list[list[int]] = []

    async def _read(self, slots=None):
        scope = sorted(self.managed_slots if slots is None else slots)
        windows.append(scope)
        return {
            slot: (
                SlotCredential.known("0000")
                if slot in (1, 2, 3)
                else SlotCredential.empty()
            )
            for slot in scope
        }

    flow_id = await _start_config_flow(hass)
    await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(flow_id, {"next_step_id": "ui"})

    with patch.object(MockLCMLock, "async_get_usercodes", _read):
        result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
            flow_id, {CONF_NUM_USERS: 2}
        )
        for name in ("Raman", "Alice"):
            result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
                flow_id, {CONF_NAME: name, CONF_ENABLED: True, CONF_PIN: "1111"}
            )

    assert result["type"] == "create_entry"
    # Slots 1-3 are taken, so the two users land on 4 and 5.
    assert result["data"][CONF_SLOT_ASSIGNMENT] == {"alice": 4, "raman": 5}
    # Every number issued was one that was actually read -- not merely one
    # below the highest read, which would let a gap through if the read ever
    # stops being contiguous.
    assert set(result["data"][CONF_SLOT_ASSIGNMENT].values()) <= {
        slot for window in windows for slot in window
    }
    # Asked about 1-2, then only 3-4, then only 5: every index once, and
    # never about the lock's whole capacity.
    assert windows == [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5]]

########## test_a_nearly_full_lock_is_read_once_through  [1598-1641]
async def test_a_nearly_full_lock_is_read_once_through(
    hass: HomeAssistant, mock_lock_config_entry
):
    """No index is asked about twice, however many passes it takes.

    Widening from the count re-reading everything each pass costs a lock
    holding codes low down several times its own capacity to place a couple
    of users -- on the providers that answer one index per round trip, that
    is the cost this whole approach exists to avoid.
    """
    asked: list[int] = []
    occupied = set(range(1, 30))

    async def _read(self, slots=None):
        scope = sorted(self.managed_slots if slots is None else slots)
        asked.extend(scope)
        return {
            slot: (
                SlotCredential.known("0000")
                if slot in occupied
                else SlotCredential.empty()
            )
            for slot in scope
        }

    flow_id = await _start_config_flow(hass)
    await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(flow_id, {"next_step_id": "ui"})

    with patch.object(MockLCMLock, "async_get_usercodes", _read):
        result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
            flow_id, {CONF_NUM_USERS: 2}
        )

    assert result["step_id"] == "code_slot"
    # The users land on 30 and 31, so 31 indices are read -- each exactly once.
    assert sorted(asked) == list(range(1, 32))
    assert len(asked) == len(set(asked)), "an index was read more than once"

    for name in ("Raman", "Alice"):
        result = await hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(
            flow_id, {CONF_NAME: name, CONF_ENABLED: True, CONF_PIN: "1111"}
        )
    assert result["type"] == "create_entry"
    assert set(result["data"][CONF_SLOT_ASSIGNMENT].values()) <= set(asked)

Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.
content.activeForm: Moving the user model onto subentries

content.subject: Task 1: Validation core (domain/validation.py)
content.description: Constants + async_validate_credential + ValidationResult + unit tests, TDD. Precedence: most restrictive wins (user_disabled > condition_not_met).

content.subject: Task 2: ReaderLock provider + dispatch
content.description: providers/reader.py subclassing VirtualLock, non-lock-domain dispatch in resolve_provider_class_for_entity, state listener, tests.

content.subject: Task 3: Config flow readers selector
content.description: Optional readers field (sensor/text) on user + options steps, merge into CONF_LOCKS, at_least_one error, strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 4: validate_code service
content.description: Service registration with SupportsResponse.OPTIONAL, multi-entry handling, services.yaml + strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 5: Property test validation ⇔ active sensor
content.description: Hypothesis property test in tests/properties/ asserting validation agrees with active binary sensor.

content.subject: Task 6: Reader E2E + full suite verification
content.description: Full-stack reader E2E incl. mixed entry, websocket/strategy tolerance check, full pytest + prek, 100% coverage.

content.subject: Task 7: Wiki page + issue comment (post-merge)
content.description: Keypad/PIN-only wiki page (no RFID yet, decided 2026-08-25) and #1414 comment describing both options.

content.subject: Fix final-review criticals and importants
content.description: Critical 1 shared-instance multi-entry; Critical 2 ATTR_STATE cleartext; Imp 3 stale revalidation; Imp 4 diagnostics; Imp 5 normalization; Minor precedence duplication.

content.subject: Update PR #1475 title and description
content.description: Retitle for use_credential + unified event + blueprint; rewrite body (currently describes validate_code as a pure query, which is two designs stale).

content.subject: Update README for shipped items
content.description: Add credential_used.yaml to the automation-blueprint list; add a feature bullet for validating codes entered outside LCM-managed locks. Direction/roadmap stays out.

content.subject: Rewrite wiki External-Keypads page
content.description: Currently documents validate_code as a pure query with no events. Needs use_credential (source/target required), the unified event, and the new blueprint. Staged unpushed until merge.

content.subject: Refresh session handoff doc
content.description: docs/2026-08-25-session-handoff-1414.md describes the design as of stages 1-5 planned; update to what actually shipped.

content.subject: Verify all three PR titles and descriptions before handoff
content.description: #1485, #1486, #1487 — read each description against its actual final diff, not against the agent's report. #1487 especially: title and body predate the operation field, credential-type event_types, and the limiter input.

content.subject: Run code review on #1489 after fixes land
content.description: Fix agent a55956239d83904a5 is applying the three Important findings (declaration exit, orphan pruning, misleading copy) plus the registryless-entity minor. Run /code-review on 1489 once it commits and pushes.

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.
content.activeForm: Moving the user model onto subentries

content.subject: Task 1: Validation core (domain/validation.py)
content.description: Constants + async_validate_credential + ValidationResult + unit tests, TDD. Precedence: most restrictive wins (user_disabled > condition_not_met).

content.subject: Task 2: ReaderLock provider + dispatch
content.description: providers/reader.py subclassing VirtualLock, non-lock-domain dispatch in resolve_provider_class_for_entity, state listener, tests.

content.subject: Task 3: Config flow readers selector
content.description: Optional readers field (sensor/text) on user + options steps, merge into CONF_LOCKS, at_least_one error, strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 4: validate_code service
content.description: Service registration with SupportsResponse.OPTIONAL, multi-entry handling, services.yaml + strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 5: Property test validation ⇔ active sensor
content.description: Hypothesis property test in tests/properties/ asserting validation agrees with active binary sensor.

content.subject: Task 6: Reader E2E + full suite verification
content.description: Full-stack reader E2E incl. mixed entry, websocket/strategy tolerance check, full pytest + prek, 100% coverage.

content.subject: Task 7: Wiki page + issue comment (post-merge)
content.description: Keypad/PIN-only wiki page (no RFID yet, decided 2026-08-25) and #1414 comment describing both options.

content.subject: Fix final-review criticals and importants
content.description: Critical 1 shared-instance multi-entry; Critical 2 ATTR_STATE cleartext; Imp 3 stale revalidation; Imp 4 diagnostics; Imp 5 normalization; Minor precedence duplication.

content.subject: Update PR #1475 title and description
content.description: Retitle for use_credential + unified event + blueprint; rewrite body (currently describes validate_code as a pure query, which is two designs stale).

content.subject: Update README for shipped items
content.description: Add credential_used.yaml to the automation-blueprint list; add a feature bullet for validating codes entered outside LCM-managed locks. Direction/roadmap stays out.

content.subject: Rewrite wiki External-Keypads page
content.description: Currently documents validate_code as a pure query with no events. Needs use_credential (source/target required), the unified event, and the new blueprint. Staged unpushed until merge.

content.subject: Refresh session handoff doc
content.description: docs/2026-08-25-session-handoff-1414.md describes the design as of stages 1-5 planned; update to what actually shipped.

content.subject: Verify all three PR titles and descriptions before handoff
content.description: #1485, #1486, #1487 — read each description against its actual final diff, not against the agent's report. #1487 especially: title and body predate the operation field, credential-type event_types, and the limiter input.

content.subject: Run code review on #1489 after fixes land
content.description: Fix agent a55956239d83904a5 is applying the three Important findings (declaration exit, orphan pruning, misleading copy) plus the registryless-entity minor. Run /code-review on 1489 once it commits and pushes.

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

The slot number survives as internal bookkeeping and NOBODY IS
    RENUMBERED: it is the credential index on most providers, so a changed
    number moves that person's code to a different index on every lock and
    orphans their entities.
    """
    config_entry = MockConfigEntry(
        domain=DOMAIN,
        data={
            CONF_LOCKS: [LOCK_1_ENTITY_ID],
            CONF_SLOTS: {
                1: {CONF_ENABLED: True, CONF_PIN: "1234"},
                2: {CONF_NAME: "Raman", CONF_ENABLED: True, CONF_PIN: "5678"},
                3: {CONF_NAME: "Raman", CONF_ENABLED: True, CONF_PIN: "9012"},
                4: {CONF_NAME: "Ra|man", CONF_ENABLED: True, CONF_PIN: "3456"},
            },
        },
        unique_id="Name Migration Test",
        version=3,
    )
    config_entry.add_to_hass(hass)

    await hass.config_entries.async_setup(config_entry.entry_id)
    await hass.async_block_till_done()

    assert config_entry.version == 5
    config = get_entry_config(config_entry)

    # Names: repaired where they had to be, untouched where they did not.
    by_slot = {num: slot[CONF_NAME] for num, slot in config.slots.items()}
    assert by_slot[1] == "User 1"  # was unnamed
    assert by_slot[2] == "Raman"  # user's choice, untouched
    assert by_slot[3] == "Raman 2"  # collided with slot 2
    assert by_slot[4] == "Ra|man"  # "|" is ordinary text now

    # Shape: keyed by user, with the slot number demoted to bookkeeping.
    stored = {**config_entry.data, **config_entry.options}
    assert CONF_SLOTS not in stored
    assert set(stored[CONF_USERS]) == {"User 1", "Raman", "Raman 2", "Ra|man"}
    # Nobody was renumbered, and the name is no longer a field of the user.
    assert stored[CONF_SLOT_ASSIGNMENT] == {
        "user 1": 1,
        "raman": 2,
        "raman 2": 3,
        "ra|man": 4,
    }
    assert CONF_NAME not in stored[CONF_USERS]["Raman"]
    # Every other field survives.
    assert stored[CONF_USERS]["User 1"][CONF_PIN] == "1234"


async def test_the_user_shape_survives_a_full_setup_cycle(
    hass: HomeAssistant, mock_lock_config_entry, lock_code_manager_config_entry
) -> None:
    """The migrated shape is still on disk after setup has written the entry back.

    Setup does not leave the entry alone: it moves data into options, the
    update listener rebuilds the configuration, and the listener's terminal
    write persists whatever ``EntryConfig.to_dict()`` emits. A to_dict that
    dropped the bookkeeping would silently rewrite the entry back to the
    slot-keyed shape on every single load.

    Nothing else catches that. Behaviour is IDENTICAL either way, because the
    integration still works in slot numbers internally -- so every behavioural
    test passes while the migration quietly undoes itself. Verified by
    mutation: removing the passthrough from to_dict leaves the whole suite
    green without this test.
    """
    stored = {
        **lock_code_manager_config_entry.data,
        **lock_code_manager_config_entry.options,
    }

    assert CONF_SLOTS not in stored
    assert set(stored[CONF_USERS]) == {"test1", "test2"}
    assert stored[CONF_SLOT_ASSIGNMENT] == {"test1": 1, "test2": 2}
    # And the reconstructed view still sees them, so nothing downstream broke.
    assert set(get_entry_config(lock_code_manager_config_entry).slots) == {1, 2}


async def test_setup_reclaims_entities_left_on_a_split_device(
    hass: HomeAssistant, mock_lock_config_entry
) -> None:
    """Entities parked on a copy of the lock's device are brought home.

    HA 2026.8 restricted a device to one config entry and split every device
    that had two, leaving a Lock Code Manager-owned copy of the lock holding
    the per-lock entities. Setup moves them onto their slot device and drops
    the emptied copy, which nothing else will: ``dr.async_cleanup`` keeps any
    device that references a live config entry, occupied or not.
    """

content.subject: Task 1: Validation core (domain/validation.py)
content.description: Constants + async_validate_credential + ValidationResult + unit tests, TDD. Precedence: most restrictive wins (user_disabled > condition_not_met).

content.subject: Task 2: ReaderLock provider + dispatch
content.description: providers/reader.py subclassing VirtualLock, non-lock-domain dispatch in resolve_provider_class_for_entity, state listener, tests.

content.subject: Task 3: Config flow readers selector
content.description: Optional readers field (sensor/text) on user + options steps, merge into CONF_LOCKS, at_least_one error, strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 4: validate_code service
content.description: Service registration with SupportsResponse.OPTIONAL, multi-entry handling, services.yaml + strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 5: Property test validation ⇔ active sensor
content.description: Hypothesis property test in tests/properties/ asserting validation agrees with active binary sensor.

content.subject: Task 6: Reader E2E + full suite verification
content.description: Full-stack reader E2E incl. mixed entry, websocket/strategy tolerance check, full pytest + prek, 100% coverage.

content.subject: Task 7: Wiki page + issue comment (post-merge)
content.description: Keypad/PIN-only wiki page (no RFID yet, decided 2026-08-25) and #1414 comment describing both options.

content.subject: Fix final-review criticals and importants
content.description: Critical 1 shared-instance multi-entry; Critical 2 ATTR_STATE cleartext; Imp 3 stale revalidation; Imp 4 diagnostics; Imp 5 normalization; Minor precedence duplication.

content.subject: Update PR #1475 title and description
content.description: Retitle for use_credential + unified event + blueprint; rewrite body (currently describes validate_code as a pure query, which is two designs stale).

content.subject: Update README for shipped items
content.description: Add credential_used.yaml to the automation-blueprint list; add a feature bullet for validating codes entered outside LCM-managed locks. Direction/roadmap stays out.

content.subject: Rewrite wiki External-Keypads page
content.description: Currently documents validate_code as a pure query with no events. Needs use_credential (source/target required), the unified event, and the new blueprint. Staged unpushed until merge.

content.subject: Refresh session handoff doc
content.description: docs/2026-08-25-session-handoff-1414.md describes the design as of stages 1-5 planned; update to what actually shipped.

content.subject: Verify all three PR titles and descriptions before handoff
content.description: #1485, #1486, #1487 — read each description against its actual final diff, not against the agent's report. #1487 especially: title and body predate the operation field, credential-type event_types, and the limiter input.

content.subject: Run code review on #1489 after fixes land
content.description: Fix agent a55956239d83904a5 is applying the three Important findings (declaration exit, orphan pruning, misleading copy) plus the registryless-entity minor. Run /code-review on 1489 once it commits and pushes.

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)

All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Real defect found by the test: `async_write_entry_config` wrote the entry half to `data`, but `from_entry` reads locks **options-first**. Any entry with staged options would keep its old locks forever after such a write — and since the diff then shows no change, the listener early-returns and never settles the options away. The listener already enforces "data is the home, options is transient staging"; the new write path has to enforce the same thing.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

content.subject: Task 1: Validation core (domain/validation.py)
content.description: Constants + async_validate_credential + ValidationResult + unit tests, TDD. Precedence: most restrictive wins (user_disabled > condition_not_met).

content.subject: Task 2: ReaderLock provider + dispatch
content.description: providers/reader.py subclassing VirtualLock, non-lock-domain dispatch in resolve_provider_class_for_entity, state listener, tests.

content.subject: Task 3: Config flow readers selector
content.description: Optional readers field (sensor/text) on user + options steps, merge into CONF_LOCKS, at_least_one error, strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 4: validate_code service
content.description: Service registration with SupportsResponse.OPTIONAL, multi-entry handling, services.yaml + strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 5: Property test validation ⇔ active sensor
content.description: Hypothesis property test in tests/properties/ asserting validation agrees with active binary sensor.

content.subject: Task 6: Reader E2E + full suite verification
content.description: Full-stack reader E2E incl. mixed entry, websocket/strategy tolerance check, full pytest + prek, 100% coverage.

content.subject: Task 7: Wiki page + issue comment (post-merge)
content.description: Keypad/PIN-only wiki page (no RFID yet, decided 2026-08-25) and #1414 comment describing both options.

content.subject: Fix final-review criticals and importants
content.description: Critical 1 shared-instance multi-entry; Critical 2 ATTR_STATE cleartext; Imp 3 stale revalidation; Imp 4 diagnostics; Imp 5 normalization; Minor precedence duplication.

content.subject: Update PR #1475 title and description
content.description: Retitle for use_credential + unified event + blueprint; rewrite body (currently describes validate_code as a pure query, which is two designs stale).

content.subject: Update README for shipped items
content.description: Add credential_used.yaml to the automation-blueprint list; add a feature bullet for validating codes entered outside LCM-managed locks. Direction/roadmap stays out.

content.subject: Rewrite wiki External-Keypads page
content.description: Currently documents validate_code as a pure query with no events. Needs use_credential (source/target required), the unified event, and the new blueprint. Staged unpushed until merge.

content.subject: Refresh session handoff doc
content.description: docs/2026-08-25-session-handoff-1414.md describes the design as of stages 1-5 planned; update to what actually shipped.

content.subject: Verify all three PR titles and descriptions before handoff
content.description: #1485, #1486, #1487 — read each description against its actual final diff, not against the agent's report. #1487 especially: title and body predate the operation field, credential-type event_types, and the limiter input.

content.subject: Run code review on #1489 after fixes land
content.description: Fix agent a55956239d83904a5 is applying the three Important findings (declaration exit, orphan pruning, misleading copy) plus the registryless-entity minor. Run /code-review on 1489 once it commits and pushes.

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.
