input.command:
cat > /tmp/pr2.md <<'EOF'
# Breaking change

The **Condition Linker** blueprint now takes the person's **Name** instead of a **Slot number**. An automation already created from it has to be reconfigured — or, since it is a one-shot, simply recreated and run.

## Proposed change

`blueprints/automation/lock_code_manager/condition_linker.yaml` still called `lock_code_manager.set_slot_condition`, removed in #1507. Anyone who had imported it got an automation that parses fine and fails at run time.

Its replacement, `set_condition`, addresses a person by name rather than a slot number, so the blueprint's input changes with it.

### Why this shipped

Nothing type-checks a blueprint. `test_blueprints.py` validated the schema and `test_blueprint_docs.py` cross-checked the documented inputs, but neither knew whether the actions being called existed. So #1507 removed four actions with a green suite while leaving a caller behind.

This adds that check: every `lock_code_manager.*` action a blueprint calls must exist in `services.yaml`, with all of that action's `required` fields supplied. Verified against both failure modes by mutation:

- restoring `set_slot_condition` → *"condition_linker.yaml calls unknown action lock_code_manager.set_slot_condition"*
- passing `slot:` instead of `name:` → *"condition_linker.yaml calls lock_code_manager.set_condition without ['name']"*

The second is the one worth having. An action that keeps its name but changes how it addresses its subject is exactly the change a schema test sees nothing wrong with.

I checked the other six blueprints: `calendar_pin_setter` and `calendar_condition` still take a slot number, but they use it to *locate an entity* by its `code_slot` attribute rather than to call a slot-addressed action, so both are unaffected.

## Type of change

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information

- Follow-up to #1507.
- `BLUEPRINTS.md` updated to match; the wiki's Blueprints page is staged alongside the other v6 wiki changes.
- Full suite green at 100% coverage; `prek` clean.
EOF
gh pr create --base v6 --head fix/blueprint-uses-removed-action --title "fix: condition linker blueprint called a removed action" --body-file /tmp/pr2.md 2>&1 | tail -2

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

Done. **PR #1511** → `v6`: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/1511

**The fix**: `condition_linker.yaml` now calls `set_condition` and takes a **Name** instead of a **Slot number**, since the replacement action addresses a person rather than a position. `BLUEPRINTS.md` updated to match — which `test_blueprint_docs.py` immediately enforced when I renamed the input, so that guard is doing its job.

**The test that would have caught it**, in `tests/test_blueprints.py`: every `lock_code_manager.*` action a blueprint calls must exist in `services.yaml`, with all of that action's `required` fields supplied. Mutation-verified on both failure modes:

- restoring `set_slot_condition` → *"condition_linker.yaml calls unknown action lock_code_manager.set_slot_condition"*
- passing `slot:` instead of `name:` → *"condition_linker.yaml calls lock_code_manager.set_condition without ['name']"*

The second one is the one that matters. An action keeping its name while changing how it addresses its subject is invisible to a schema test — and that's the half of #1507 that a simple "does this action exist" check would still have missed.

I swept the other six blueprints: `calendar_pin_setter` and `calendar_condition` still take a slot number, but they use it to *locate an entity* via the `code_slot` attribute rather than to call a slot-addressed action, so both are fine. No other stale references in `blueprints/`.

Full suite green at 100% coverage (2297), `prek` clean.

**Where things stand:**

| | |
|---|---|
| #1510 | users as subentries → `v6` |
| #1511 | blueprint fix + the guard → `v6` |
| wiki | 5 files staged, uncommitted |
| prod | restored to 5.4.0 / v4, verified |

The wiki now includes `Blueprints.md`, since the code backs that claim — I'd left it alone earlier rather than document an intent the file didn't have.

Two things still open for you: whether the add-user card keeps its own dialog now that the native page does add/edit/delete, and the wiki commit message once you've read the staged diff.

cat > /tmp/pr-v6.md <<'EOF'
# Breaking change

**Four actions removed.** They addressed a lock slot or a device instead of a person:

| Removed | Use instead |
|---|---|
| `lock_code_manager.set_usercode` | [`set_credential`](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Services-and-Actions#set_credential) |
| `lock_code_manager.clear_usercode` | [`clear_credential`](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Services-and-Actions#clear_credential) |
| `lock_code_manager.set_slot_condition` | [`set_condition`](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Services-and-Actions#set_condition) |
| `lock_code_manager.clear_slot_condition` | [`clear_condition`](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/wiki/Services-and-Actions#clear_condition) |

**The `lock_code_manager_lock_state_changed` event is removed.** Use `lock_code_manager_credential_used`, which names the *person* rather than the slot number they occupy. Field-by-field mapping is on the wiki.

**Users are now config subentries.** A v4 → v5 migration moves them on load. Nothing is renamed and nobody is renumbered, so every entity keeps its ID, its settings and its history. The **Configure** screen now edits only the locks; each user gets their own add, edit and delete dialog on the entry's page, with their entities and device grouped under them.

**The Condition Linker blueprint takes a Name instead of a Slot number.** An automation already created from it must be reconfigured, or simply recreated — it is a one-shot.

## Proposed change

The through-line is that a *person* is the unit Lock Code Manager works in, and the slot number is internal bookkeeping. Every surface that leaked that number is gone: the four slot-addressed actions, the lock-shaped event, and the `slot_assignment` side table.

Users move into config subentries, so each person's slot number lives in their own record and the configuration can no longer disagree with itself about who holds which. `async_write_entry_config` is the single write path, matching users **by slot number** — not by name, which is what a rename changes.

### Verified against a real instance

Deployed to a production instance holding two v4 entries and restored from a full backup afterwards. Both migrated to v5, users landed in subentries with their numbers intact, and all 31 entities plus all 3 slot devices came up bound to the right person — no duplicates, no orphans, no errors.

That run caught two things the suite could not, both fixed here:

- Home Assistant deprecates letting `async_add_entities` drag an existing device into a subentry. Every *upgrading* instance is in that position, since its devices predate subentries; the suite creates devices fresh during setup, already bound, so only a real upgrade reproduces it. The migration now moves each one with `async_update_device`.
- A Lovelace card cannot open Home Assistant's subentry dialog: `dialog-data-entry-flow` ships only in lazily-loaded chunks, and no URL starts a subentry flow. The add-user card keeps its own dialog and links to the page that hosts the native ones.

### Defects this exposed

Five bugs that were latent before this branch:

1. **The unmanaged-code sweep ran mid-migration.** It asks every entry what it manages; part-way through the chain an entry's users were still in `data`, so it saw zero managed slots and would have raised a repair for every one of its *own* codes on any v3 upgrade.
2. **`from_entry` reads the entry's locks options-first**, so writing only `data` was invisible whenever options were staged — and, showing no diff, never woke the listener that clears them.
3. **The update listener's terminal settle corrupted multi-write sequences.** Reconciling subentries and the entry takes several calls, each waking the listener; a pass waking between them wrote back the half it had read.
4. **A rename destroyed the user.** Matching subentries by identity — derived from the name — made a rename read as a departure plus an arrival. Harmless until entities were bound; then removing the subentry would take that person's entities, settings and history.
5. **A blueprint called a removed action.** `condition_linker` went on calling `set_slot_condition` with a green suite, because nothing type-checks a blueprint. There is now a test that every action a blueprint calls exists in `services.yaml` with its required fields supplied.

## Type of change

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (which adds functionality)
- [x] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information

- Rolls up #1507, #1508, #1510 and #1511. Part of #1481.
- 65 files, +1,704 / −2,057 — a net reduction, mostly from the removed surfaces and the tests that covered them.
- Full suite green at 100% coverage; `prek` clean.
- Wiki updates for all of the above are prepared separately.
EOF
gh pr create --base main --head v6 --title "feat!: a person is the unit — users as subentries, slot-addressed surfaces removed" --body-file /tmp/pr-v6.md 2>&1 | tail -2

Read files at `origin/v6` (e.g. `git show origin/v6:path/to/file.py`), NOT the working tree — the working tree is on a different branch.

**Focus: correctness and data-loss risk.** This PR moves each "user" of a config entry out of `entry.data` and into a Home Assistant **config subentry**, with a v4→v5 migration. It also removes four deprecated services and one deprecated event.

Concentrate on:

1. **`async_migrate_entry` in `custom_components/lock_code_manager/__init__.py`.** This is a one-way door — there is no code-level rollback, recovery is a backup restore. Look hard at ordering between the v1→v5 steps, partial-failure behaviour, and anything that reads entry state mid-chain (which would see a half-migrated shape).
2. **`async_write_entry_config` in `domain/config.py`.** It reconciles subentries and the entry in several separate calls, each of which wakes the update listener. Look for sequences where a listener waking between two of those writes observes an inconsistent state, and for any path that could remove a subentry (which takes its entities, devices and history with it) when it meant to update one.
3. **`_async_apply_entry_update` in `__init__.py`** — the update listener. It diffs a cached config against the current one and early-returns when there is no diff. Check the caching, the recursion guard, and the `if config_entry.options:` settle at the end.
4. **`EntryConfig.from_entry`** — reads locks options-first but users from subentries. Look for places where those two halves can disagree.
5. The **subentry flow** and **options flow** in `config_flow.py`, especially slot allocation when adding a user and slot preservation when editing one.

Report only issues you are confident are real, with file:line and a concrete failure scenario (specific inputs/state → wrong outcome). Do not report style, naming, or missing tests unless a missing test hides a live bug. If you find nothing real, say so plainly — a clean report is a valid result.

content.subject: Task 1: Validation core (domain/validation.py)
content.description: Constants + async_validate_credential + ValidationResult + unit tests, TDD. Precedence: most restrictive wins (user_disabled > condition_not_met).

content.subject: Task 2: ReaderLock provider + dispatch

content.subject: Task 3: Config flow readers selector

content.subject: Task 4: validate_code service
content.description: Service registration with SupportsResponse.OPTIONAL, multi-entry handling, services.yaml + strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 5: Property test validation ⇔ active sensor
content.description: Hypothesis property test in tests/properties/ asserting validation agrees with active binary sensor.

content.subject: Task 6: Reader E2E + full suite verification
content.description: Full-stack reader E2E incl. mixed entry, websocket/strategy tolerance check, full pytest + prek, 100% coverage.

content.subject: Task 7: Wiki page + issue comment (post-merge)
content.description: Keypad/PIN-only wiki page (no RFID yet, decided 2026-08-25) and #1414 comment describing both options.

content.subject: Fix final-review criticals and importants
content.description: Critical 1 shared-instance multi-entry; Critical 2 ATTR_STATE cleartext; Imp 3 stale revalidation; Imp 4 diagnostics; Imp 5 normalization; Minor precedence duplication.

content.description: Retitle for use_credential + unified event + blueprint; rewrite body (currently describes validate_code as a pure query, which is two designs stale).

content.subject: Update README for shipped items
content.description: Add credential_used.yaml to the automation-blueprint list; add a feature bullet for validating codes entered outside LCM-managed locks. Direction/roadmap stays out.

content.subject: Rewrite wiki External-Keypads page
content.description: Currently documents validate_code as a pure query with no events. Needs use_credential (source/target required), the unified event, and the new blueprint. Staged unpushed until merge.

content.subject: Refresh session handoff doc
content.description: docs/2026-08-25-session-handoff-1414.md describes the design as of stages 1-5 planned; update to what actually shipped.

content.description: #1485, #1486, #1487 — read each description against its actual final diff, not against the agent's report. #1487 especially: title and body predate the operation field, credential-type event_types, and the limiter input.

content.subject: Run code review on #1489 after fixes land
content.description: Fix agent a55956239d83904a5 is applying the three Important findings (declaration exit, orphan pruning, misleading copy) plus the registryless-entity minor. Run /code-review on 1489 once it commits and pushes.

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.
content.activeForm: Moving the user model onto subentries

content.text:
**PR #1514** is open: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/1514 — `v6` → `main`, titled `feat!: a person is the unit — users as subentries, slot-addressed surfaces removed`.

It rolls up #1507, #1508, #1510 and #1511: **65 files, +1,704 / −2,057** — a net reduction, since the removed surfaces and their tests outweigh the subentry work. The body leads with the breaking changes as a migration table (four removed actions → their replacements, the removed event → `credential_used` with field mapping, users → subentries, the blueprint's `Slot number` → `Name`), then the prod verification and the five latent defects the move exposed.

`breaking-change` label applied correctly — the auto-tagger keyed on the section, as expected.

**CI**: 10 of 14 green (Hassfest, Mypy, Ruff, pre-commit.ci, both labelers, Check Changes, Setup, Release Draft). Frontend Vitest, Yarn Build, HACS and Pytest 3.14 still running.

**Two review passes are running now** over the full `main...v6` diff, deliberately non-overlapping:

1. **Correctness / data-loss** — the migration chain as a one-way door, `async_write_entry_config`'s multi-write sequence and whether a listener waking mid-sequence can observe an inconsistent state, the listener's caching and settle gate, and slot allocation in the subentry flow.
2. **Silent failures and orphaned callers** — sweeping every *non-Python* shipped file (blueprints, `services.yaml`, `strings.json`, `translations/en.json`, `icons.json`, the TS, README/BLUEPRINTS) in both directions: references to things that no longer exist, and things that exist but are no longer referenced. That's the class that already bit us once with the blueprint, and it's the one a green suite doesn't cover.

I'll report what they find when they're back. Separately, worth knowing: four worktrees are now merged and stale (`blueprint-fix`, `subentries`, `v6-event`, `v6-remove`) — say the word and I'll clear them out.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

content.subject: Task 5: Property test validation ⇔ active sensor
content.description: Hypothesis property test in tests/properties/ asserting validation agrees with active binary sensor.

content.description: Add credential_used.yaml to the automation-blueprint list; add a feature bullet for validating codes entered outside LCM-managed locks. Direction/roadmap stays out.

content.description: Currently documents validate_code as a pure query with no events. Needs use_credential (source/target required), the unified event, and the new blueprint. Staged unpushed until merge.

content.description: #1485, #1486, #1487 — read each description against its actual final diff, not against the agent's report. #1487 especially: title and body predate the operation field, credential-type event_types, and the limiter input.

content.description: Fix agent a55956239d83904a5 is applying the three Important findings (declaration exit, orphan pruning, misleading copy) plus the registryless-entity minor. Run /code-review on 1489 once it commits and pushes.

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

content.description: #1485, #1486, #1487 — read each description against its actual final diff, not against the agent's report. #1487 especially: title and body predate the operation field, credential-type event_types, and the limiter input.

content.subject: Run code review on #1489 after fixes land
content.description: Fix agent a55956239d83904a5 is applying the three Important findings (declaration exit, orphan pruning, misleading copy) plus the registryless-entity minor. Run /code-review on 1489 once it commits and pushes.

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. Full suite is green (2301 passed). Every finding below was reproduced with a probe test against the real HA harness, then the probes were deleted.

## Critical

### 1. The migration's device re-parenting never finds a real device (confidence 97)

`custom_components/lock_code_manager/__init__.py:461-465`

```python
device = dev_reg.async_get_device(
    identifiers={
        build_slot_device_identifier(config_entry.entry_id, slot_num)
    }
)
```

`build_slot_device_identifier` returns a bare string (`"{entry_id}|{slot}"`). HA's device registry keys on `(domain, identifier)` tuples, and production slot devices are created that way — `entity.py:56-57` uses `identifiers={(DOMAIN, build_slot_device_identifier(...))}`, as do `__init__.py:1305`, `:1476` and `:1576`. So this lookup returns `None` for every device and the whole `if device is not None` block is dead.

**Failure scenario, reproduced:** v4 entry, one user "Housekeeper" at slot 1, with the slot device already in the registry under `(DOMAIN, "{entry_id}|1")` owned by the entry and no subentry. After `async_migrate_entry` runs, the device is still `{entry_id: {None}}` — the deliberate move did not happen. Setup then continues and the device gets dragged into the subentry implicitly by `async_add_entities`, which is precisely the path the code comment says it exists to avoid. HA logs:

> Detected that custom integration 'lock_code_manager' assigns an existing device to a different config subentry, by calling `async_get_or_create` or by adding entities from several subentries that share a device; this silently moves the device. … at `custom_components/lock_code_manager/binary_sensor.py`, line 54. **This will stop working in Home Assistant 2027.8.0**, please create a bug report

Every upgrading instance hits this on first load. Side effect of the implicit move: `entity_registry.async_device_modified` sees `config_subentry_id` change from `None` and calls `async_remove` on every pre-existing entity on that device; they are restored from `deleted_entities` on re-add, so in my probe names/entity_ids survived — but that restore depends on each entity being recreated in the same pass, which is not guaranteed for a lock that fails to set up.

Fix: `identifiers={(DOMAIN, build_slot_device_identifier(config_entry.entry_id, slot_num))}`.

**Why the tests don't catch it:** `tests/test_init.py:2114 test_migration_v5_moves_an_existing_slot_device_to_its_user` builds its fixture device with the *same* wrong identifier shape (`identifiers={build_slot_device_identifier(config_entry.entry_id, 1)}`), so the assertion passes against a device shape production never creates. Worth fixing the fixture to `(DOMAIN, ...)` in the same change — the test then fails until the code is fixed.

Note: `diagnostics.py:171-173` has the identical missing-tuple shape, but it is unchanged by this PR (pre-existing).

## Important

### 2. Four allocation errors have no string in the new subentry flow (confidence 92)

`custom_components/lock_code_manager/config_flow.py:757-762` surfaces `_allocate_for`'s refusals as `errors = {"base": err.translation_key}`. `domain/allocation.py` can raise `too_many_users`, `numbers_needed_exceed_capacity`, `search_limit_reached`, `occupancy_unknown` and `slot_out_of_range`.

`strings.json` `config_subentries.user.error` (line 515-522) defines only `missing_pin_if_enabled`, `name_not_unique`, `name_required`, `excluded_platform`, `slot_out_of_range`, `slots_already_configured`. The first four keys above are missing (they *are* present under `config.error` and `options.error`).

**Failure scenario:** entry manages a 30-slot lock that is already full; user clicks "Add user" and submits. `async_allocate_for` raises `too_many_users`, the form re-renders with `{"base": "too_many_users"}`, and the frontend has nothing to render — the user sees the raw key instead of "…the lock only has N slots…". Same for a lock that is asleep (`occupancy_unknown`), the most likely one in practice.

`tests/test_config_flow.py:2049` (`test_editing_refuses_when_a_lock_cannot_be_read`) asserts exactly `{"base": "occupancy_unknown"}` on this flow and passes — it checks the key the code produced, not that a string exists for it. Copying the four entries from `config.error` into `config_subentries.user.error` fixes it; a test that asserts every key the flow can emit is present in `strings.json` would keep it fixed.

## Minor (reporting because you asked about these specific sites)

### 3. `if config_entry.options:` never runs when the options flow is a no-op edit (confidence 88, low impact)

`__init__.py:1862` returns before the settle at `:2030` whenever the diff is empty. Reproduced: set up an entry with `locks=[lock.test_1]`, open the options flow, resubmit the same lock. `async_create_entry` writes `options={'locks': ['lock.test_1']}`, the listener finds no lock/slot delta and early-returns, and the entry is left with `data == options == {'locks': ['lock.test_1']}` indefinitely.

I could not construct harm from it: the only writer of `options` is the options flow, which writes `{**extra, locks}`, and every other write path (`async_write_entry_config`, the settle, reauth, migration) clears options, so the leftover is always byte-identical to `data` and is swept on the next real change or restart. Flagging it only because the comment above the guard states an invariant ("everything else writes `data` directly and clears `options` itself") that the options flow itself violates on this path, and a future options-flow field that *isn't* also in `data` would make it a real staleness bug.

### 4. `subentry.data[CONF_SLOT]` raises `KeyError` on a subentry with no number (confidence 90, reachability low)

`config_flow.py:815`. Reproduced: entry with one normal user plus `unnumbered_user_subentry("Nomad", enabled=False)` (the helper `tests/common.py:494` documents this state as reachable from "hand-edited storage or a half-finished write"). Opening "Edit user" on Nomad renders the form fine, then submitting raises `KeyError: 'slot'` out of the flow — the user gets "Unknown error occurred" with no way forward and no way to delete-and-recreate from that dialog. `subentry.data.get(CONF_SLOT)` plus a guard (or re-allocating) would degrade gracefully.

### 5. Docs still promise the removed `lock_state_changed` event (confidence 95, docs-only)

`BLUEPRINTS.md:322` — "They all still travel on the deprecated `lock_code_manager_lock_state_changed` bus event, **which keeps firing**" — and `AGENTS.md:124-135` §7, which describes it as "retained for backward compatibility … with no removal version set". Commit 745d7780 removes it (`grep EVENT_LOCK_STATE_CHANGED custom_components/` is empty). A user reading the breaking-change note in BLUEPRINTS.md is told the fields they lost are still available somewhere they are not.

## Checked and found sound

- **Migration ordering.** `sweep_unmanaged` is captured from `config_entry.version` at the top and deferred to the bottom, so the sweep reads a fully-migrated entry — correct, and the chain never re-reads entry state through a reader that assumes the new shape mid-flight. Probed both real-world v3 and v4 steady states (`data={}`, everything in `options`); both land at version 5 with `data={'locks': [...]}`, `options={}`, users intact.
- **`async_write_entry_config` removal path.** Matching on the slot number rather than the name is right: a rename through the name text entity (`slot_coordinator._write_config_fields({CONF_NAME: ...})` → `with_user_renamed`, which re-keys the assignment too) hits the same key and takes the `async_update_subentry` branch. Probed: subentry_id, all entity_ids and the device survive a rename; `entry_users` shows only the new name.
- **Listener re-entrancy.** `hass.async_create_task` defaults to `eager_start=True`, so the update listener *does* run inline between the subentry writes and the entry write in `async_write_entry_config`. It is defused by `EntryConfig.to_dict()` no longer carrying users — a mid-write settle can only rewrite `extra + locks`, which are unchanged by every production caller of `async_write_entry_config`.
- **Deleting a user's subentry from the UI.** `async_remove_subentry` → listener → `slots_removed` → entity removers, device removal, `async_release_managed_slot`. Probed with two users: the departing user's entities all go, the other user's are untouched.
- **Duplicate slot numbers across two subentries** (which `SlotAssignment.__post_init__` de-dupes, leaving the loser with no number): I expected the next `async_write_entry_config` to destroy the loser's subentry. It does not — the dict-comprehension collision in `existing` means nothing is left over to remove; you get a spurious extra unnumbered subentry instead. Messy, but not destructive, and I found no production path that creates the duplicate.
- **Concurrent "Add user" subentry flows** (two flows opened, both submitted under `asyncio.gather`): no duplicate slot numbers issued.
- Websocket command renames are consistent between `websocket.py`, `ts/*.ts` and the generated bundle; `services.yaml`, `strings.json` and the registered services all agree after the four removals; the condition-linker blueprint now calls `set_condition` with `name`.</result>

content.subject: Task 1: Validation core (domain/validation.py)
content.description: Constants + async_validate_credential + ValidationResult + unit tests, TDD. Precedence: most restrictive wins (user_disabled > condition_not_met).

content.subject: Task 2: ReaderLock provider + dispatch
content.description: providers/reader.py subclassing VirtualLock, non-lock-domain dispatch in resolve_provider_class_for_entity, state listener, tests.

content.subject: Task 3: Config flow readers selector
content.description: Optional readers field (sensor/text) on user + options steps, merge into CONF_LOCKS, at_least_one error, strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 4: validate_code service
content.description: Service registration with SupportsResponse.OPTIONAL, multi-entry handling, services.yaml + strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 5: Property test validation ⇔ active sensor
content.description: Hypothesis property test in tests/properties/ asserting validation agrees with active binary sensor.

content.subject: Task 6: Reader E2E + full suite verification
content.description: Full-stack reader E2E incl. mixed entry, websocket/strategy tolerance check, full pytest + prek, 100% coverage.

content.subject: Task 7: Wiki page + issue comment (post-merge)
content.description: Keypad/PIN-only wiki page (no RFID yet, decided 2026-08-25) and #1414 comment describing both options.

content.subject: Fix final-review criticals and importants
content.description: Critical 1 shared-instance multi-entry; Critical 2 ATTR_STATE cleartext; Imp 3 stale revalidation; Imp 4 diagnostics; Imp 5 normalization; Minor precedence duplication.

content.subject: Update PR #1475 title and description
content.description: Retitle for use_credential + unified event + blueprint; rewrite body (currently describes validate_code as a pure query, which is two designs stale).

content.subject: Update README for shipped items
content.description: Add credential_used.yaml to the automation-blueprint list; add a feature bullet for validating codes entered outside LCM-managed locks. Direction/roadmap stays out.

content.subject: Rewrite wiki External-Keypads page
content.description: Currently documents validate_code as a pure query with no events. Needs use_credential (source/target required), the unified event, and the new blueprint. Staged unpushed until merge.

content.subject: Refresh session handoff doc
content.description: docs/2026-08-25-session-handoff-1414.md describes the design as of stages 1-5 planned; update to what actually shipped.

content.subject: Verify all three PR titles and descriptions before handoff
content.description: #1485, #1486, #1487 — read each description against its actual final diff, not against the agent's report. #1487 especially: title and body predate the operation field, credential-type event_types, and the limiter input.

content.description: Fix agent a55956239d83904a5 is applying the three Important findings (declaration exit, orphan pruning, misleading copy) plus the registryless-entity minor. Run /code-review on 1489 once it commits and pushes.

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store

cat > /tmp/pr3.md <<'EOF'
# Breaking change

None. Every change here fixes something already on `v6`.

## Proposed change

Two independent review passes over #1514 agreed on the same critical, plus three smaller findings. Each fix comes with the guard that would have caught it.

### 1. The migration's device move never found a device

`__init__.py` looked slot devices up as `identifiers={build_slot_device_identifier(...)}` — a bare string. The device registry keys on `(domain, identifier)` tuples, which is how `entity.py` and every other call site creates them. The lookup returned `None` for every device, so the whole block was dead and **every upgrading instance took the deprecated implicit path** that block exists to avoid: one `assigns an existing device to a different config subentry` warning per slot device on every start, and a hard failure on HA Core 2027.8.

**Its test could not have caught it.** The test built its fixture device with the *same* malformed identifier the buggy code searched for, so the two agreed with each other and disagreed with production. It now registers the device through the same `DeviceInfo` the entities carry.

Correcting the identifier alone was still not enough: with the fixture fixed, the test *still* passed against the broken lookup, because a full setup adds the user's entities and those drag the device across by themselves. The end state is identical whether the migration moved the device or not. The test now exercises `async_migrate_entry` on its own, which is the only way to observe the difference.

### 2. Four allocation refusals had no sentence in the subentry flow

`config_subentries.user.error` was missing `too_many_users`, `numbers_needed_exceed_capacity`, `search_limit_reached` and `occupancy_unknown`. Adding a user is now the *only* way to add a user, so a full lock or a sleeping one — the likeliest refusal in practice — showed the bare translation key.

Guard: a test that reads every `SlotAllocationError` key out of `allocation.py` and asserts each flow that allocates has a sentence for it. Read from the source rather than listed, so it cannot go stale.

Also pruned `options.error` to the one key the locks-only options flow can still produce.

### 3. Editing a user who holds no number raised out of the dialog

`subentry.data[CONF_SLOT]` in the reconfigure step. Not a state the integration writes — hand-edited storage or a half-finished write leaves one — but it meant the one record a user might need to repair was the one record the UI could not touch. It now issues a number, or refuses cleanly if the lock cannot be read.

### 4. The shipped card was keeping a back-compat shim alive

`add-user-card.ts` called `add_user` with the flat pre-6.0 shape, which works only through `_flat_user_to_list`. Removing that shim would have broken the Add User button, and no frontend test would have said so — they mock `callService`, so nothing on that side ever meets the schema. The card now sends the declared `users: [...]` shape, with a contract test asserting it.

### 5. Docs promised a removed event still fires

`BLUEPRINTS.md` and `AGENTS.md` both said `lock_code_manager_lock_state_changed` "keeps firing" / is "retained for backward compatibility". It was removed in #1508. `BLUEPRINTS.md`'s claim sat inside the breaking-change note explaining where to recover the fields the entity dropped — pointing users at an event that never fires.

### Also

Corrected a comment in the update listener that stated an invariant the options flow can violate: an options submission that changes nothing returns before the settle, leaving `options` standing. Harmless while `options` only ever holds `data`'s own contents, which is now noted at the site so nobody adds a field that breaks it.

## Type of change

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information

- Follow-up to #1514. Every fix mutation-verified: each new guard fails against the code it is meant to catch.
- Full suite green at 100% coverage (2306); frontend 820; `prek` clean.
EOF

content.text:
Both reviews are running. Here's the options concern, concretely.

## The convention

A HA config entry has two dicts. LCM treats them as: **`data` is the home, `options` is a staging area.** The options flow can't write `data` directly — HA hands its result to `options` — so the update listener folds `options` into `data` and clears it. Everything else (`async_write_entry_config`, the migration, entity edits) writes `data` and sets `options={}` itself.

What makes staging work is that `EntryConfig.from_entry` reads the locks **options-first**:

```python
locks=tuple(entry.options.get(CONF_LOCKS, entry.data.get(CONF_LOCKS, [])))
```

So between the flow writing and the listener settling, readers already see the new locks.

## The hole

The listener does this, in order (`__init__.py`):

```
1868  diff = EntryConfigDiff(old=old_config, new=new_config)
1869  if not diff.has_changes:
1870      return                          ← early return
...    entity / device work
2043  if config_entry.options:            ← the settle
2044      async_update_entry(data=..., options={})
```

The settle is at the **bottom**, behind a diff that only knows about slots and locks. Open the options flow, change nothing, hit save: HA writes `options = {locks: [...], **extra}`, the listener wakes, the diff is empty, it returns at line 1870 — and never reaches line 2043. **`options` stays populated permanently**, across restarts.

## Why it's inert today

The options flow writes `{**config.extra, CONF_LOCKS: user_input[CONF_LOCKS]}`. On a no-op submission that is byte-identical to `data`. Options-first reads therefore return exactly the same answer, forever. No observable difference — which is why neither reviewer could construct harm from it, and why I left it.

## Why I flagged it anyway

The failure mode isn't the stale copy, it's what happens *later*. Any subsequent `async_write_entry_config` does `data=config.to_dict(), options={}`. So a value living **only** in `options` gets silently erased on the next unrelated edit.

That can't happen while the options flow's payload is a strict subset of `data`. It becomes real the moment someone adds an options-flow field that isn't also in `data` — a genuinely natural thing to do, since that's what an options flow is normally *for*. The trap is that it would work perfectly in testing (options-first reads find it) and vanish the first time a user renamed somebody.

## The fix, if you want it closed

Move the settle **above** the diff, gated the same way:

```python
if config_entry.options:
    async_update_entry(config_entry, data=new_config.to_dict(), options={})
    return          # the write re-enters with a settled entry
diff = EntryConfigDiff(...)
```

Then the diff is always computed on a settled entry and `options` is never a place anything lives. It's safe against the multi-write hazard that put the settle at the bottom in the first place — during `async_write_entry_config`'s sequence, `options` is empty, so the new gate never fires mid-sequence.

I'd call it a 10-line change plus a test that a no-op options submission leaves `options` empty. Your call whether it belongs in v6 or after — it's latent either way, and closing it now costs less than the comment I left explaining why it's fine.

async def _async_apply_entry_update(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    config_entry: LockCodeManagerConfigEntry,
    old_config: EntryConfig | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Bring entities, devices and locks into line with the entry."""
    # Refresh the cached EntryConfig on EVERY update — including entity-driven
    # writes that go straight to data with empty options (e.g. a slot's name or
    # PIN being edited via its text entity). The early-return below skips the
    # entity-creation pass for those cases, but downstream readers via
    # runtime_data.config still need to see the current data.
    runtime_data = config_entry.runtime_data
    # What the entry looked like when this pass started, captured before the
    # refresh below overwrites it. Users live in subentries and locks may be
    # on either side, so comparing the cached view against the current one
    # is the only comparison that sees both.
    # ``None`` means "compare against what we last saw". Setup passes an empty
    # config instead, because at that point nothing has been created yet and
    # every user is new -- diffing against the cache would find no changes and
    # build nothing.
    if old_config is None:
        old_config = runtime_data.config
    runtime_data.config = new_config = EntryConfig.from_entry(config_entry)

    # Notify per-slot coordinators so derived "active" state and condition-
    # entity subscriptions stay in sync with the refreshed config view.
    # Runs on both the entity-driven path (early return below) and the
    # options-flow path so a calendar/condition swap is picked up the
    # same way.
    for coordinator in runtime_data.slot_coordinators.values():
        coordinator.notify_config_changed()

    _async_rename_slot_devices(hass, config_entry)

    # Nothing changed means nothing to do -- which also makes this its own
    # recursion guard, because the settle write at the end of this function
    # produces no diff when it re-enters.
    diff = EntryConfigDiff(old=old_config, new=new_config)
    if not diff.has_changes:
        return

    ent_reg = er.async_get(hass)

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

    `data` is where the configuration lives; `options` is a staging area,

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.
content.activeForm: Moving the user model onto subentries

## Critical: the unnumbered-edit path asks allocation for one user too many

**Confidence: 95.** `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/config_flow.py:824` and `:833` (at `c170ad9f`; now also on `v6` at `d082ef4b`).

```python
) = await _allocate_for(
    self.hass, entry, config.locks, len(config.users) + 1
)
...
held_slot = config.assignment.reconcile(
    {**config.users, name: fields}, start=1, unavailable=unavailable
).slot(name)
```

The `+ 1` was copied from `async_step_user` (add), where it is correct because `config.users` does not yet contain the newcomer. In `async_step_reconfigure` it **does** — `EntryConfig.from_entry` (`domain/config.py:138`) puts every user subentry into `users` regardless of whether it carries `CONF_SLOT`; only `assignment` skips the unnumbered one. So the user being repaired is counted twice.

I confirmed both symptoms by instrumenting the flow:

**Symptom A — the repair dialog refuses on a lock that has room.** Entry with `Alice` (slot 1) + unnumbered `Nomad`, lock advertising 2 PIN slots, slot 2 free:

```
type=form errors={'base': 'too_many_users'}
ph={'lock': 'lock.test_1', 'num_slots': '2', 'num_users': '3', 'out_of_range_slots': '3'}
```

Two users exist, the lock holds two, and the user is told *"Lock lock.test_1 has 2 PIN code slots, so 3 users will not fit."* This is exactly the failure the fix's own comment says it exists to prevent — *"a dialog that can only fail leaves the user with no way to repair the record from the UI"* — reintroduced at the capacity boundary, with a message naming a user count that does not exist.

**Symptom B — renaming during the repair burns a slot.** Sole unnumbered user `Nomad`, renamed to `Zed`, empty lock:

```
type=abort title=Zed data={'enabled': True, 'pin': '4242', 'slot': 2}
```

`reconcile` sees `{nomad, zed}` (the stale `held` key plus the new name), assigns alphabetically, and hands `Zed` slot 2 while slot 1 is left permanently unused. Same root cause: the edited user is in the dict twice.

**Fix** — exclude the record being edited, exactly as `_validate_user_form`'s `taken` argument already does two lines above:

```python
others = {other: user for other, user in config.users.items() if other != held}
...
) = await _allocate_for(self.hass, entry, config.locks, len(others) + 1)
...
held_slot = config.assignment.reconcile(
    {**others, name: fields}, start=1, unavailable=unavailable
).slot(name)
```

The existing two tests pass either way — `test_editing_a_user_who_has_no_number_issues_one` has one user on an empty lock, where `2` and `1` allocate identically, and no test renames during the repair. Both scenarios above are worth adding.
