cat > /tmp/pr4.md <<'EOF'
# Breaking change

None. Both fixes are to code already on `v6`.

## Proposed change

### 1. A no-op options submission stranded itself in `options`

`data` is where an entry's configuration lives; `options` is a staging area, because an options flow cannot write `data` itself. The update listener is what keeps that true — it folds `options` into `data` and clears it.

That settle sat at the bottom of the listener, behind an early return for "nothing changed". So opening the options flow and saving without changing anything left the submission staged **permanently**, across restarts.

Inert today: what the options flow writes is a strict subset of `data`, and `EntryConfig.from_entry` reads those keys options-first, so both sides always agreed. It stops being inert the moment an options-flow field exists that *isn't* also in `data` — which is what an options flow is normally for. Such a field would read correctly (options-first) and then be silently erased by the next write that touched the entry, since every other write does `data=..., options={}`.

Settling is now one `_async_settle_options` helper called from both exits, rather than a block at the bottom that one path skips.

I did **not** move the settle to the top of the listener, which was the obvious-looking fix: the re-entrant pass would diff against a cache the outer pass had already refreshed, and at setup — which passes `EntryConfig.empty()` as the old config — it would skip entity creation entirely.

### 2. The unnumbered-user repair counted that user twice

`async_step_reconfigure` asked allocation for `len(config.users) + 1`. The `+ 1` was carried over from the add flow, where it is right because the newcomer is not in `config.users` yet. On the edit path they are — `EntryConfig.from_entry` puts every user subentry into `users` whether or not it carries a slot; only `assignment` skips the unnumbered one.

Two consequences, both reproduced:

- **On a lock with exactly enough room, the repair refused.** Entry with `Alice` on slot 1 plus an unnumbered `Nomad`, lock with 2 slots: `{"base": "too_many_users"}`, telling the user *"3 users will not fit"* when there are two. Exactly the failure this path was added to prevent — a dialog that can only fail — reintroduced at the capacity boundary.
- **A repair that also renamed burned a slot.** `reconcile` was handed a dict still containing the old name alongside the new one, so the same person appeared twice under two identities and the new name was numbered around the old one, leaving slot 1 permanently unused.

Both now read from one `others` dict — everybody except the person being edited — which is what the name-uniqueness check two lines above already used.

The existing tests passed either way: the one test on this path has a single user on an empty lock, where `2` and `1` allocate identically, and nothing renamed during a repair. Both scenarios are now covered, and both fail against the old arithmetic.

## Type of change

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [x] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information

- Follow-up to #1515, found by a review pass over it. Every new test mutation-verified.
- Full suite green at 100% coverage (2309); `prek` clean.
EOF

content.text:
**PR #1516** → `v6`: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/1516

Two things in it, because the review of #1515 caught a bug in my own fix from that PR.

**The options settle** — done as you asked. One `_async_settle_options` helper, called from both exits of the listener instead of a block at the bottom that the early-return skipped.

Worth flagging: **the obvious fix was wrong.** Moving the settle to the top of the listener looks cleaner, but the settle write re-enters the listener inline, and by then the outer pass has already refreshed `runtime_data.config` — so the re-entrant pass would diff a config against itself and find nothing. At setup, which passes `EntryConfig.empty()` as the old config precisely so everything looks new, it would have skipped entity creation entirely. Settling on both exits leaves all the existing ordering intact.

**The bug the review found in my #1515 fix.** The unnumbered-user repair asked allocation for `len(config.users) + 1`. I copied the `+ 1` from the *add* flow, where it's right because the newcomer isn't in `config.users` yet. On the *edit* path they are — `from_entry` puts every user subentry into `users` whether or not it carries a slot. So the person being repaired was counted twice:

- On a lock with exactly enough room, the repair **refused**: *"3 users will not fit"* when two exist. That is the exact failure the path was added to prevent — a dialog that can only fail — reintroduced at the capacity boundary.
- A repair that also renamed put the same person in twice under two identities, numbered the new name around the old one, and burned slot 1 for good.

My two tests passed either way: one user on an empty lock, where `2` and `1` allocate identically, and nothing renamed. Both scenarios are now covered and both fail against the old arithmetic. The fix routes everything through one `others` dict — which is what the name-uniqueness check two lines above already used, so the correct exclusion was sitting right there.

The reviewer also verified the four other #1515 fixes hold up, and specifically that their guards aren't vacuous — including re-applying the malformed device identifier to confirm the migration test now genuinely fails.

Note `origin/v6` moved to `d082ef4b` while this ran — you merged #1515, so I rebased onto it.

The second review (delete paths, slot reuse, reload/restart, concurrency across the whole 65-file diff) is still running; I'll report when it lands.

## 1. HIGH — `clear_credentials: false` only honours the first name

`/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/__init__.py:1946-1947`

```python
retained_pairs = runtime_data.retained_pairs
runtime_data.retained_pairs = set()
```

`async_delete_users` stages every departing user's `(lock, slot)` pairs into `runtime_data.retained_pairs` (`domain/services.py:581`) and then makes **one** call to `async_write_entry_config`. But that function is now N writes, not one: `domain/config.py:647` calls `async_remove_subentry` once per departing user, and HA's `_async_update_entry` starts each update listener as an **eager** task. So pass 1 begins executing inside the *first* `async_remove_subentry`, drains the whole `retained_pairs` set, and matches it against a diff that contains only the first user. Pass 2 (started inside the second `async_remove_subentry`) finds `retained_pairs` empty and calls `async_release_managed_slot` on the second user's slot.

Reproduced: entry with `Guest0` (slot 3) and `Guest1` (slot 4), two locks.

```yaml
action: lock_code_manager.delete_user
data:
  config_entry_id: ...
  name: [Guest0, Guest1]
  clear_credentials: false
```

`async_release_managed_slot` was called with `[4, 4]` — Guest1's PIN was wiped from both locks despite the explicit hand-off. Guest0's was correctly retained. The service is documented as "Lock Code Manager stops managing those slots and whatever is programmed there keeps working"; for everyone after the first it does the opposite, irreversibly.

The fix is to discard pairs as they are consumed rather than draining wholesale — e.g. `runtime_data.retained_pairs -= diff.pairs_removed` after the loop, keeping the rest for the passes still to come.

---

## 2. HIGH — deleting a user while the entry is unloaded leaves the PIN on the lock

`/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/__init__.py:946-947`

The only thing that clears a departing user's credential is the update listener, and it is registered in `_setup_entry_after_start` and torn down by `async_on_unload`. HA's `async_remove_subentry` has no integration hook — it removes the subentry, the entities and the device, and schedules `entry.update_listeners`, which is empty when the entry is not loaded. v6 is the first release where a user can be deleted without going through LCM code at all; in v5 both routes (`delete_user` service via `get_loaded_config_entry`, and the options flow via `_allocate_for`) required a loaded entry.

Reproduced: set up the entry, `async_unload`, `async_remove_subentry` for `test1` (slot 1), reload. After reload the lock still reports `{1: SlotCredential(present=True, pin='1234')}` and no entry manages slot 1. The same applies to a disabled entry, and to one sitting in `SETUP_ERROR` — which is exactly the state reauth exists for, so "lock entity missing → reauth → user tidies up the roster while they're in there" is a plausible path.

Nothing recovers it: `async_sweep_unmanaged_codes` runs only from `async_migrate_entry`, and the setup pass diffs against `EntryConfig.empty()` so `pairs_removed` is always empty. The PIN keeps opening the door and the slot number is burned (allocation refuses a number it can still read a code on). This is the `#1453` failure mode through a new door.

`_async_prune_orphaned_slot_devices` (`__init__.py:1593`) already computes the exact signal at setup — slot devices whose number is no longer configured — so the cheapest fix is to release those pairs on the locks before pruning the devices.

---

`async_delete_users` stages every departing user's `(lock, slot)` pairs into `runtime_data.retained_pairs` (`domain/services.py:581`) and then makes **one** call to `async_write_entry_config`. action: lock_code_manager.delete_user
data:
  config_entry_id: ...

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

def _async_prune_orphaned_slot_devices(
    hass: HomeAssistant, config_entry: LockCodeManagerConfigEntry
) -> None:
    """
    Drop slot devices left behind by a slot that is no longer in config.

    Runs at setup so registries already polluted by the pre-fix behavior get
    cleaned up on the next reload, rather than only newly-removed slots
    benefiting. Sweeps by identifier rather than by diffing against a
    previous config, so it also catches slots removed while the entry was
    unloaded.
    """
    dev_reg = dr.async_get(hass)
    entry_id = config_entry.entry_id
    configured = get_entry_config(config_entry).slot_numbers
    orphaned = {
        slot_num
        for device in dr.async_entries_for_config_entry(dev_reg, entry_id)
        for domain, identifier in device.identifiers
        if domain == DOMAIN
        and (slot_num := parse_slot_device_identifier(entry_id, identifier)) is not None
        and slot_num not in configured
    }
    if orphaned:
        _LOGGER.debug(
            "%s (%s): Pruning devices for unconfigured slots %s",
            entry_id,
            config_entry.title,
            sorted(orphaned),
        )
        _async_remove_slot_devices(hass, config_entry, orphaned)


async def async_remove_config_entry_device(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    config_entry: LockCodeManagerConfigEntry,
    device_entry: dr.DeviceEntry,
) -> bool:
    """
    Allow deleting a slot device from the UI, but only once it is unused.

    Home Assistant renders the device's Delete button only when this hook
    exists, which is why there was previously no way to clear a stale slot
    device (issue #1399). A device whose slot is still configured must stay:
    deleting it would strand the slot's entities, and the next reload would
    recreate it anyway.
    """
    entry_id = config_entry.entry_id
    slot_nums = {
        slot_num
        for domain, identifier in device_entry.identifiers
        if domain == DOMAIN
        and (slot_num := parse_slot_device_identifier(entry_id, identifier)) is not None
    }
    # No slot identifier means this is the entry's own device, which has to
    # outlive every slot -- it is what the slot devices hang off of.
    if not slot_nums:
        return False

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

**A batch hand-off only honoured the first name.** \`delete_user\` with \`clear_credentials: false\` stages every departing user's \`(lock, slot)\` pairs, then makes one call to \`async_write_entry_config\` — which is now N writes, one subentry removal per user, each waking the listener eagerly. The listener drained the whole set on its first pass, so from the second user onward the credential the caller explicitly asked to leave programmed was wiped off every lock. Reproduced: deleting two users with \`clear_credentials: false\` released slot 2 anyway. Pairs are consumed per-pass now.

**The reclaim path created its slot device with no subentry**, so the pre-2026.8 upgrade path took the deprecated implicit move — on the exact upgrade v6 is aimed at. Also dropped \`OPERATION_SOURCE_NAMES\` in the ZHA provider, dead since the \`lock_state_changed\` removal.

---

Two findings from that pass are **not** in this PR, and both are worth a decision rather than a rushed fix.

**Deleting a user while the entry is unloaded leaves the PIN on the lock.** HA's \`async_remove_subentry\` has no integration hook, so a user removed from the entry's page while it is unloaded, disabled, or in setup-error is removed without any LCM code running. Nothing notices afterwards — the setup pass diffs against an empty config, where \`pairs_removed\` is empty by construction. The PIN keeps opening the door and the slot is burned, since allocation will not reissue a number it can still read a code on. This is the #1453 failure mode through a door v6 opens.

I tried the obvious remedy — release the slots whose *device* outlived their configuration, which \`_async_prune_orphaned_slot_devices\` already computes at setup — and **it detects nothing**, because HA removes the device along with the subentry. That signal does not exist in v6 precisely because devices are now subentry-bound. I reverted it rather than ship a fix that does nothing.

What is left is a design call: run \`async_sweep_unmanaged_codes\` at every setup (raises a repair per unmanaged code, so the user decides rather than having a code cleared out from under them — but reads every lock on every start), or persist the managed slot set and diff it at setup (cheap and exact, but adds stored state).

**\`_async_write_and_settle\` releases early on batches.** \`settled\` is set by whichever listener pass finishes first, not the last, so a multi-name \`add_user\`/\`delete_user\` can return while later passes are still writing. The docstring already concedes a concurrent write can release the wait early — but that was written when one logical operation meant one pass. Both existing tests use a single name. content.text:
The second review found four more. Two are fixed and pushed to **#1516**; two need your call.

**Fixed and pushed:**

**A batch hand-off only honoured the first name.** `delete_user` with `clear_credentials: false` stages every departing user's pairs, then makes one call to `async_write_entry_config` — which is now N writes, one subentry removal per user, each waking the listener eagerly. The listener drained the whole set on its first pass, so from the second user onward the credential you explicitly asked to leave programmed got wiped off every lock. Reproduced, fixed, mutation-verified. Same root cause as the settle bug: one logical operation is no longer one pass.

**The reclaim path created its slot device with no subentry**, taking the deprecated implicit move on exactly the pre-2026.8 upgrade v6 targets. Plus `OPERATION_SOURCE_NAMES` in the ZHA provider, dead since the event removal.

**Not fixed, and this is the important one:**

**Deleting a user while the entry is unloaded leaves the PIN on the lock.** HA's `async_remove_subentry` has no integration hook, so a user removed from the entry's page while the entry is unloaded, disabled, or in setup-error is removed with no LCM code running. Nothing catches it afterwards — the setup pass diffs against an empty config, where `pairs_removed` is empty by construction. The PIN keeps opening the door and the slot is burned. That's #1453 through a door v6 opens.

I implemented the reviewer's suggested remedy — release slots whose *device* outlived their config, which the setup prune already computes — and **it detected nothing**. HA removes the device along with the subentry, so that signal doesn't exist in v6, precisely *because* I made devices subentry-bound. I reverted it rather than ship a fix that does nothing; that's the same class of dead-code-that-looks-like-a-fix as the device-identifier bug earlier today.

Two real options, and the tradeoff is yours:

- **Sweep at setup** — run `async_sweep_unmanaged_codes` on every load. Raises a repair per unmanaged code, so the user decides rather than having a code cleared out from under them (which matters: a deliberate hand-off looks identical). Cost: reads every lock on every start.
- **Persist the managed slot set** and diff at setup. Cheap and exact, but adds stored state to the entry.

I lean toward the sweep — it surfaces rather than acts, and setup already reads the locks — but the per-start cost on a sleepy Z-Wave mesh is a real objection.

**Also open:** `_async_write_and_settle` releases on whichever listener pass finishes first, so a multi-name `add_user`/`delete_user` can return while later passes are still writing. Both existing tests use a single name. Fix is to have `async_write_entry_config` report how many entry updates it made so the waiter counts them — maybe 20 lines, but I didn't want to change settle semantics without you seeing it.

Both are written up on #1516.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

# LCM v6: users as config subentries — what shipped and what it cost

PRs: #1510 (model move), #1511 (blueprint fix + guard), #1514 (v6→main), #1515 (review fixes), #1516 (follow-ups).

## The model

Each user of a config entry is a `ConfigSubentry` of type `"user"`, carrying their own
credential position in `data[CONF_SLOT]`. The `slot_assignment` side table is gone, so the
configuration can no longer disagree with itself about who holds which number.

- `EntryConfig.from_entry` reads users from `entry.subentries`, locks from the entry
  (options-first, because the options flow stages there).
- `async_write_entry_config` is the single write path. **Users are matched to subentries by
  SLOT NUMBER, not by name** — matching by name makes a rename read as a departure plus an
  arrival, and `async_remove_subentry` takes the person's entities, settings and history.
- The options flow edits locks only. Add/edit/delete a user goes through
  `LockCodeManagerUserSubentryFlow` on the entry's own page.
- Entities and devices carry `config_subentry_id`, which is what makes HA group them under
  the person rather than in one flat list.

## Verified on production, then restored

Full backup `aeb056fb` → rsync branch → `docker restart homeassistant` → observe → full restore.
Two v4 entries migrated to v5; users landed in subentries with numbers intact; 31/31 entities
and 3/3 slot devices bound to the right person; no duplicates, no errors. Restore confirmed:
manifest back to 5.4.0, both entries back to version 4.

Prod caught two things the suite structurally could not:

1. HA deprecates letting `async_add_entities` drag an *existing* device into a subentry.
   Every UPGRADING instance is in that position (its devices predate subentries); the suite
   creates devices fresh during setup, already bound, so only a real upgrade reproduces it.
2. A Lovelace card cannot open HA's subentry dialog at all (see below).

## A Lovelace card cannot open the native subentry dialog

Checked against the installed frontend: `dialog-data-entry-flow` exists only in numbered
(lazy) chunks a dashboard has no reason to have pulled in, and an unregistered custom element
renders as nothing rather than failing. There is also **no URL that starts a subentry flow** —
the only deep link is `/config/integrations/integration/<domain>#config_entry=<id>`.

So the add-user card keeps its own dialog and links to the page that hosts the native ones.

## Five latent defects the move exposed

1. **The unmanaged-code sweep ran mid-migration.** It asks every entry what it manages;
   part-way through the chain an entry's users were still in `data`, so it saw zero managed
   slots and would have raised a repair for every one of its OWN codes on any v3 upgrade.
   Moved to the end of `async_migrate_entry`, gated on the incoming version.
2. **`from_entry` reads locks options-first**, so a `data`-only write was invisible whenever
   options were staged — and, showing no diff, never woke the listener that clears them.
3. **The listener's terminal settle corrupted multi-write sequences.** A pass waking between
   two of `async_write_entry_config`'s writes wrote back the half it had read.
4. **A rename destroyed the user** (identity-matching, above).
5. **A blueprint called a removed action** with a green suite, because nothing type-checks a
   blueprint.

## "One logical operation is no longer one listener pass"

This single shift caused three separate bugs. `async_write_entry_config` makes N writes (one
subentry removal/update per user, plus the entry), and HA starts update listeners EAGERLY —
they run inline, mid-sequence.

- The settle corruption above.
- **`retained_pairs` drained wholesale.** `delete_user` with `clear_credentials: false` stages
  every departing user's pairs, then makes one call. The listener took the whole set on its
  first pass, so from the second user onward the credential the caller explicitly asked to
  leave programmed was wiped off every lock. Now consumed per pair
  (`retained_pairs - diff.pairs_removed`).
- **`_async_write_and_settle` releases on the first pass, not the last** — a multi-name
  service can return while later passes are still writing. STILL OPEN.

## Still open (Raman's call)

**Deleting a user while the entry is unloaded leaves the PIN on the lock.** HA's
`async_remove_subentry` has no integration hook, so a user removed from the entry's page while
the entry is unloaded/disabled/in setup-error is removed with no LCM code running. Nothing
catches it after: the setup pass diffs against `EntryConfig.empty()`, where `pairs_removed` is
empty by construction. The PIN keeps opening the door and the slot is burned (allocation will
not reissue a number it can still read a code on). This is the #1453 failure mode through a
door v6 opens.

The obvious remedy — release slots whose *device* outlived their configuration, which
`_async_prune_orphaned_slot_devices` already computes at setup — **detects nothing**, because
HA removes the device along with the subentry. That signal does not exist in v6 precisely
because devices are now subentry-bound. Reverted rather than ship a fix that does nothing.

Options: run `async_sweep_unmanaged_codes` at every setup (raises a repair per unmanaged code,
so the user decides rather than having a code cleared out from under them — a deliberate
hand-off looks identical — but reads every lock on every start), or persist the managed slot
set and diff at setup (cheap and exact, adds stored state).

# When a mutation check proves nothing: two ways it lied in one session

Both incidents were in code I had already reported to Raman as "mutation-verified".

## 1. The fixture agreed with the bug

A migration looked devices up as `identifiers={build_slot_device_identifier(...)}` — a bare
string. Home Assistant's device registry keys on `(domain, identifier)` TUPLES, which is how
every other call site creates them. The lookup matched nothing, so the whole block was dead,
and every upgrading instance silently took the deprecated path the block existed to avoid.

My test built its fixture device with the SAME malformed identifier. Bug and fixture agreed
with each other and disagreed with production. Deleting the block made the test fail — which
felt like proof, but only proved the mutation reached the TEST's invariant.

**Rule:** build fixtures through the production constructor (here `build_slot_device_info`,
the same `DeviceInfo` the entities carry), never by hand-assembling the identifier. This was
the third incident of a test validating its own assumption.

## 2. Something downstream repaired the damage

Correcting the fixture to the tuple form STILL passed. A full `async_setup` adds the user's
entities, and adding entities re-parents the device by itself — so the end state is identical
whether the migration moved it or not. Only calling `async_migrate_entry` ALONE could observe
the difference.

**Rule:** when a mutation "passes", ask what else in the system produces the same end state.
If something downstream repairs it, the test is measuring the repair, not the code. Isolate
the unit that owns the invariant.

## 3. The corollary — a fix copied from a sibling path

Separately: an "unnumbered user repair" path asked allocation for `len(config.users) + 1`.
The `+1` was correct in the ADD flow it was copied from, where the newcomer is not yet in
`users`. On the EDIT path they are, so the person was counted twice — the repair dialog
refused on a lock with exactly enough room (the very failure the path was added to prevent),
and a rename during repair burned a slot.

Both of my tests passed either way: one user on an empty lock, where `N` and `N+1` allocate
identically, and nothing renamed. **A test that cannot distinguish the off-by-one is not a
test of the arithmetic.** Pick fixtures at the boundary the code actually branches on.

## What a real guard looked like

For the class "shipped config nothing type-checks" (blueprints, `services.yaml`,
`strings.json`), the checks worth writing were the ones for the SILENT variant:

- every `lock_code_manager.*` action a blueprint calls exists in `services.yaml` **AND all its
  `required` fields are supplied** — the second half catches an action that keeps its name but
  changes how it addresses its subject (slot number → name), which a schema test sees nothing
  wrong with.
- every `SlotAllocationError` translation key, READ OUT OF THE SOURCE by regex rather than
  listed, has a sentence in each flow that can raise it. Listing them would just be a second
  place to forget.

## Summary

The event-field removal is clean. I verified repo-wide that nothing still references `ATTR_ACTION_TEXT`, `ATTR_CODE_SLOT_NAME`, `ATTR_NOTIFICATION_SOURCE`, `ATTR_EXTRA_DATA`, `ATTR_FROM`/`ATTR_TO`, `ATTR_LCM_CONFIG_ENTRY_ID`, `ATTR_LOCK_CONFIG_ENTRY_ID`, `EVENT_LOCK_STATE_CHANGED`, or `_serialize_source_data` — in code, comments, blueprints, or shipped config. I ran an AST sweep for module-level constants in every provider that are now referenced ≤ once and found no other `OPERATION_SOURCE_NAMES`-style leftovers. No provider lost data it still uses: `data` (matter), `source`/`event_code` (zha), `event_label` (zwave_js_ui), `payload`/`action` (zigbee2mqtt) all still feed live logic. No provider reads a name out of a location v6 moved — `providers/` touches config in exactly one place (`_base.py:2074`, via `get_entry_config().name_for()`), and all seven `credential_used` fields are structurally guaranteed because every provider funnels through `async_fire_code_slot_event` and the base fills the payload itself.

Three findings.

---

### 1. HIGH — Matter's release path can delete a lock user LCM never created

`/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/matter.py:847` calls `_find_user_index_for_slot` (defined at `:772`), whose **second** lookup (`:808-817`) adopts *any untagged* lock user that owns a PIN credential at `cred.slot == slot`. `async_delete_user` (`:819`) then issues Matter `ClearUser`, whose spec cascade removes that user and all of its credentials.

That fallback is defensible on the *set* path — it re-adopts a pre-6.0 LCM user and rewrites its name. On the *release* path it is not symmetric: the set path's worst case is a mis-adopted user gets renamed and re-PINned; the release path's worst case is the irreversible deletion of a credential LCM never wrote.

Concrete failure: a Matter lock where the homeowner added a PIN through the manufacturer's app or Apple Home. Matter auto-allocated it credential index 1, and its user is untagged. In LCM you add "Guest", who gets slot 1, and never fill in a PIN (or the lock is offline when the write is attempted) — so no `lcm:1:` user is ever created on that lock. You then delete "Guest". `diff.pairs_removed` is purely configuration-derived (`domain/config.py:457-499`), so the release fires for a slot that never held anything. The canonical pass finds no `lcm:1:` user, the legacy pass matches the homeowner's user at credential index 1, and `ClearUser` destroys it. Nothing in LCM reports why that person is locked out.

Two amplifiers:
- The release loop runs for **every** lock in the entry, not just the one the slot was written to (`__init__.py:1996-2009`). An entry with three Matter locks fires this at all three.
- It is not idempotent in the dangerous direction: the second call for the same slot cannot find LCM's own (now-deleted) user, so it falls to the adoption pass. The docstring at `matter.py:841-845` claims it "tolerates no user found", but the fallback means that branch is often not the one taken.

Recommendation: the release path should use the canonical (tag-matched) lookup only. Give `_find_user_index_for_slot` a flag, or split out a `_find_tagged_user_index_for_slot`, and have `async_release_managed_slot` call that. Adoption belongs to the write path, which can repair a wrong guess; teardown cannot.

### 2. MEDIUM — same adoption flaw in the base default release, via `async_clear_usercode`

`providers/_base.py:1730` (`async_release_managed_slot`) → `async_internal_clear_usercode` → `async_clear_usercode`, whose native-user owner resolution has the identical two-pass structure at `_base.py:1292-1310`. The fallback at `:1301-1310` matches an **untagged** user owning a PIN at `credential.slot == code_slot`.

Reached from a *sync clear* this is correct — the slot is LCM's, and adopting the pre-tag credential is the point. Reached from `async_release_managed_slot` the premise has inverted: the slot is no longer LCM's, and there is no follow-up write to correct a wrong guess. On zwave_js under the User Credential CC, `credential_index_follows_slot` is True, so a foreign controller's user with a PIN at credential slot N is very likely to collide with LCM slot N; releasing slot N deletes that credential. Less destructive than the Matter case (credential only, not the whole user), but the same root cause.

Worth fixing together with #1 — probably a `scope` parameter on the shared resolution rather than a second resolver, per the "a second read path skips the repairs" lesson.

### 3. LOW — dead parameter left by the event-field removal (sibling of `OPERATION_SOURCE_NAMES`)

`providers/zwave_js_ui.py:648` — `_process_notification`'s `topic` parameter is now unread. Its only use was `source_data={"topic": topic, "value": value}`, deleted in this PR; the call site at `:581` still passes it. I diffed unused-argument analysis between `origin/main` and `origin/v6` across all nine providers, and this is the **only** newly-dead one — no other siblings.

---

### Note on test coverage (not a code defect)

`tests/providers/zwave_js/test_events.py` converted the three keypad-notification tests from capturing a real bus event to `zwave_js_lock.async_fire_code_slot_event = fired` plus `fired.assert_called_once_with(...)`. That is a test one level from the truth: after this change no zwave_js test proves a keypad notification produces an actual `credential_used` event on the bus. `tests/providers/test_base.py` still covers the funnel generically, so the gap is zwave_js-specific — but it is the provider whose notification decoding is most intricate, and the assertion would be equally cheap against the real event.</result>

The event-field removal is clean. I verified repo-wide that nothing still references `ATTR_ACTION_TEXT`, `ATTR_CODE_SLOT_NAME`, `ATTR_NOTIFICATION_SOURCE`, `ATTR_EXTRA_DATA`, `ATTR_FROM`/`ATTR_TO`, `ATTR_LCM_CONFIG_ENTRY_ID`, `ATTR_LOCK_CONFIG_ENTRY_ID`, `EVENT_LOCK_STATE_CHANGED`, or `_serialize_source_data` — in code, comments, blueprints, or shipped config. I ran an AST sweep for module-level constants in every provider that are now referenced ≤ once and found no other `OPERATION_SOURCE_NAMES`-style leftovers. No provider lost data it still uses: `data` (matter), `source`/`event_code` (zha), `event_label` (zwave_js_ui), `payload`/`action` (zigbee2mqtt) all still feed live logic. No provider reads a name out of a location v6 moved — `providers/` touches config in exactly one place (`_base.py:2074`, via `get_entry_config().name_for()`), and all seven `credential_used` fields are structurally guaranteed because every provider funnels through `async_fire_code_slot_event` and the base fills the payload itself.

Three findings.

---

### 1. HIGH — Matter's release path can delete a lock user LCM never created

`/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/matter.py:847` calls `_find_user_index_for_slot` (defined at `:772`), whose **second** lookup (`:808-817`) adopts *any untagged* lock user that owns a PIN credential at `cred.slot == slot`. `async_delete_user` (`:819`) then issues Matter `ClearUser`, whose spec cascade removes that user and all of its credentials.

That fallback is defensible on the *set* path — it re-adopts a pre-6.0 LCM user and rewrites its name. On the *release* path it is not symmetric: the set path's worst case is a mis-adopted user gets renamed and re-PINned; the release path's worst case is the irreversible deletion of a credential LCM never wrote.

Concrete failure: a Matter lock where the homeowner added a PIN through the manufacturer's app or Apple Home. Matter auto-allocated it credential index 1, and its user is untagged. In LCM you add "Guest", who gets slot 1, and never fill in a PIN (or the lock is offline when the write is attempted) — so no `lcm:1:` user is ever created on that lock. You then delete "Guest". `diff.pairs_removed` is purely configuration-derived (`domain/config.py:457-499`), so the release fires for a slot that never held anything. The canonical pass finds no `lcm:1:` user, the legacy pass matches the homeowner's user at credential index 1, and `ClearUser` destroys it. Nothing in LCM reports why that person is locked out.

Two amplifiers:
- The release loop runs for **every** lock in the entry, not just the one the slot was written to (`__init__.py:1996-2009`). An entry with three Matter locks fires this at all three.
- It is not idempotent in the dangerous direction: the second call for the same slot cannot find LCM's own (now-deleted) user, so it falls to the adoption pass. The docstring at `matter.py:841-845` claims it "tolerates no user found", but the fallback means that branch is often not the one taken.

Recommendation: the release path should use the canonical (tag-matched) lookup only. Give `_find_user_index_for_slot` a flag, or split out a `_find_tagged_user_index_for_slot`, and have `async_release_managed_slot` call that. Adoption belongs to the write path, which can repair a wrong guess; teardown cannot.

### 2. MEDIUM — same adoption flaw in the base default release, via `async_clear_usercode`

`providers/_base.py:1730` (`async_release_managed_slot`) → `async_internal_clear_usercode` → `async_clear_usercode`, whose native-user owner resolution has the identical two-pass structure at `_base.py:1292-1310`. The fallback at `:1301-1310` matches an **untagged** user owning a PIN at `credential.slot == code_slot`.

Reached from a *sync clear* this is correct — the slot is LCM's, and adopting the pre-tag credential is the point. Reached from `async_release_managed_slot` the premise has inverted: the slot is no longer LCM's, and there is no follow-up write to correct a wrong guess. On zwave_js under the User Credential CC, `credential_index_follows_slot` is True, so a foreign controller's user with a PIN at credential slot N is very likely to collide with LCM slot N; releasing slot N deletes that credential. Less destructive than the Matter case (credential only, not the whole user), but the same root cause.

Worth fixing together with #1 — probably a `scope` parameter on the shared resolution rather than a second resolver, per the "a second read path skips the repairs" lesson.

### 3. LOW — dead parameter left by the event-field removal (sibling of `OPERATION_SOURCE_NAMES`)

`providers/zwave_js_ui.py:648` — `_process_notification`'s `topic` parameter is now unread. Its only use was `source_data={"topic": topic, "value": value}`, deleted in this PR; the call site at `:581` still passes it. I diffed unused-argument analysis between `origin/main` and `origin/v6` across all nine providers, and this is the **only** newly-dead one — no other siblings.

async def _find_user_index_for_slot(self, slot: int) -> int | None:
        """
        Return the ``user_index`` of the user LCM owns for ``slot``, if any.

        Two lookups, in priority order:

        1. **Canonical** -- a user whose name carries the
           ``lcm:<slot>:`` tag. This is the post-PR-B identity rule.
        2. **Legacy adoption** -- an *untagged* user owning a PIN
           credential at ``credential_index == slot``. Pre-PR-B Matter
           LCM pinned ``credential_index`` to the LCM slot, so an
           untagged user owning a PIN at that index is almost certainly
           the LCM 2.0 user for this slot. Adopting it (the subsequent
           ``set_lock_user`` rewrites the name to the tagged form, and
           ``set_lock_credential`` MODIFY'es the existing credential
           index in place) preserves a single, identifiable user per
           slot across the upgrade. Without this fallback the new model
           would CREATE a second user every time, silently leaving the
           pre-upgrade PIN active on the lock.

           The legacy pass MUST skip users whose names already parse to
           ANY LCM slot. Under the new model the Matter credential index
           is auto-allocated, so a user tagged ``lcm:<A>:`` can own a
           PIN at index ``B``; matching on ``cred.slot == slot`` alone
           would mis-adopt slot-A's user as slot-B's anchor.

        Returns ``None`` when neither lookup matches.
        """
        users = await self.async_get_users()
        try:
            return next(
                existing.user_id
                for existing in users
                if existing.name and parse_tag(existing.name)[0] == slot
            )
        except StopIteration:
            return next(
                (
                    existing.user_id
                    for existing in users
                    if parse_tag(existing.name or "")[0] is None
                    for cred in existing.pin_credentials
                    if cred.slot == slot
                ),
                None,
            )

content.description: Constants + async_validate_credential + ValidationResult + unit tests, TDD. Precedence: most restrictive wins (user_disabled > condition_not_met).

content.subject: Task 2: ReaderLock provider + dispatch
content.description: providers/reader.py subclassing VirtualLock, non-lock-domain dispatch in resolve_provider_class_for_entity, state listener, tests.

content.subject: Task 3: Config flow readers selector
content.description: Optional readers field (sensor/text) on user + options steps, merge into CONF_LOCKS, at_least_one error, strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 4: validate_code service
content.description: Service registration with SupportsResponse.OPTIONAL, multi-entry handling, services.yaml + strings, tests.

content.subject: Task 5: Property test validation ⇔ active sensor
content.description: Hypothesis property test in tests/properties/ asserting validation agrees with active binary sensor.

content.subject: Task 6: Reader E2E + full suite verification
content.description: Full-stack reader E2E incl. mixed entry, websocket/strategy tolerance check, full pytest + prek, 100% coverage.

content.description: Keypad/PIN-only wiki page (no RFID yet, decided 2026-08-25) and #1414 comment describing both options.

content.subject: Fix final-review criticals and importants
content.description: Critical 1 shared-instance multi-entry; Critical 2 ATTR_STATE cleartext; Imp 3 stale revalidation; Imp 4 diagnostics; Imp 5 normalization; Minor precedence duplication.

content.description: Retitle for use_credential + unified event + blueprint; rewrite body (currently describes validate_code as a pure query, which is two designs stale).

content.subject: Update README for shipped items
content.description: Add credential_used.yaml to the automation-blueprint list; add a feature bullet for validating codes entered outside LCM-managed locks. Direction/roadmap stays out.

content.subject: Rewrite wiki External-Keypads page
content.description: Currently documents validate_code as a pure query with no events. Needs use_credential (source/target required), the unified event, and the new blueprint. Staged unpushed until merge.

content.description: docs/2026-08-25-session-handoff-1414.md describes the design as of stages 1-5 planned; update to what actually shipped.

content.subject: Verify all three PR titles and descriptions before handoff
content.description: #1485, #1486, #1487 — read each description against its actual final diff, not against the agent's report. #1487 especially: title and body predate the operation field, credential-type event_types, and the limiter input.

content.subject: Run code review on #1489 after fixes land
content.description: Fix agent a55956239d83904a5 is applying the three Important findings (declaration exit, orphan pruning, misleading copy) plus the registryless-entity minor. Run /code-review on 1489 once it commits and pushes.

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

async def test_notification_event_keypad_lock_fires_a_code_slot_event(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,
    zwave_integration: MockConfigEntry,
    lock_schlage_be469: Node,
    mock_access_control: MagicMock,
    mock_lock_helpers: dict,
) -> None:
    """Test that a keypad lock notification event reaches the code slot event funnel."""
    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(domain=DOMAIN, data={CONF_LOCKS: [], CONF_SLOTS: {}})
    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)
    await zwave_js_lock.async_setup_internal(lcm_entry)

    # Capture LCM lock state changed events
    fired = MagicMock()
    zwave_js_lock.async_fire_code_slot_event = fired

    # Create a notification event matching the pattern from Home Assistant core tests
    # Type 6 = ACCESS_CONTROL, Event 5 = KEYPAD_LOCK_OPERATION
    event = ZwaveEvent(
        type="notification",
        data={
            "source": "node",
            "event": "notification",
            "nodeId": lock_schlage_be469.node_id,
            "endpointIndex": 0,
            "ccId": 113,  # Notification CC
            "args": {
                "type": 6,  # ACCESS_CONTROL
                "event": 5,  # KEYPAD_LOCK_OPERATION
                "label": "Access Control",
                "eventLabel": "Keypad lock operation",
                "parameters": {"userId": 1},
            },
        },
    )
    lock_schlage_be469.receive_event(event)
    await hass.async_block_till_done()

    fired.assert_called_once_with(code_slot=1, to_locked=True)

    await zwave_js_lock.async_unload(False)

content.description: Retitle for use_credential + unified event + blueprint; rewrite body (currently describes validate_code as a pure query, which is two designs stale).

content.description: Add credential_used.yaml to the automation-blueprint list; add a feature bullet for validating codes entered outside LCM-managed locks. Direction/roadmap stays out.

content.description: Currently documents validate_code as a pure query with no events. Needs use_credential (source/target required), the unified event, and the new blueprint. Staged unpushed until merge.

content.description: docs/2026-08-25-session-handoff-1414.md describes the design as of stages 1-5 planned; update to what actually shipped.

content.description: #1485, #1486, #1487 — read each description against its actual final diff, not against the agent's report. #1487 especially: title and body predate the operation field, credential-type event_types, and the limiter input.

content.subject: Run code review on #1489 after fixes land
content.description: Fix agent a55956239d83904a5 is applying the three Important findings (declaration exit, orphan pruning, misleading copy) plus the registryless-entity minor. Run /code-review on 1489 once it commits and pushes.

content.subject: Revert #1492 entity lookup from use_credential
content.description: Revert commit e8fe9b77 on feat/lockless-entries: remove lock_entity_id/member_entity_id input from use_credential. Keep config_entry_id and config_entry_title (both shipped in 5.2.0; removing either is breaking). Also removes the queries.py helper and validation.py additions the commit brought in.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

content.subject: Add optional availability source field
content.description: New CONF_AVAILABILITY_ENTITIES: user-picked entities whose availability gates the entry's entities, so a lock-less entry can still follow its keypad going offline. Needs: const, EntryConfig field (from_mapping/to_dict/empty), unified source set used by _is_available AND both TrackStates call sites AND the _handle_available_state_update filter, config flow user+options steps, strings.json + translations/en.json.

content.subject: Test lock-less entries and availability sources
content.description: E2E: entry with zero locks sets up LOADED, entities live, validate_credential resolves the user, use_credential works by entry title. Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

content.subject: Run full suite and prek, open PR
content.description: Full pytest tests/ (not a subset), prek run --all-files, then open PR against feature/credential-store-model using .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Keep the description short. No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.

input.command:
cat > /tmp/issue.md <<'EOF'
## The problem

`async_release_managed_slot` — the sole route by which a departing user's lock-side state is torn down — resolves the user to delete with **find-or-adopt** logic, the same logic the *write* path uses. On the write path adoption is right and self-correcting. On the teardown path it can irreversibly delete a credential Lock Code Manager never created.

**This is not new in v6.** Both sites are on `main` today.

### Matter — deletes the whole user

`providers/matter.py:847` calls `_find_user_index_for_slot`, whose second lookup (`:808-817`) adopts **any untagged** lock user owning a PIN credential at `cred.slot == slot`. `async_delete_user` then issues Matter `ClearUser`, which per spec cascades to the user *and all of its credentials*.

Reproduction:

1. A homeowner adds a PIN through the lock manufacturer's app or Apple Home. Matter auto-allocates it credential index 1; its user is untagged.
2. In Lock Code Manager you add "Guest", who is issued slot 1, and you never give them a PIN (or the lock is offline when the write is attempted) — so no `lcm:1:` user is ever created on that lock.
3. You delete "Guest".

`diff.pairs_removed` is derived purely from configuration, so the release fires for a slot that never held anything. The canonical pass finds no `lcm:1:` user; the adoption pass matches the homeowner's user at credential index 1; `ClearUser` destroys it. **Nothing reports why that person is now locked out.**

Two amplifiers:

- The release loop runs for **every lock in the entry**, not just the one the slot was written to (`__init__.py`'s `pairs_removed` loop). An entry with three Matter locks fires this at all three.
- It is not idempotent in the dangerous direction. A second release for the same slot cannot find LCM's own (now-deleted) user, so it falls through to adoption again. The docstring's claim that it "tolerates no user found" holds only when the fallback misses.

### Base layer — deletes the credential

`providers/_base.py:1730` (`async_release_managed_slot`) → `async_internal_clear_usercode` → `async_clear_usercode`, whose native-user owner resolution has the same two-pass shape at `_base.py:1292-1310`, adopting an untagged user owning a PIN at `credential.slot == code_slot`.

Reached from a *sync clear* this is correct — the slot is LCM's, and adopting the pre-tag credential is the whole point. Reached from a *release* the premise has inverted: the slot is no longer LCM's, and there is no follow-up write to correct a wrong guess. On zwave_js under the User Credential CC `credential_index_follows_slot` is True, so a foreign controller's user holding a PIN at credential slot N is very likely to collide with LCM slot N.

Less destructive than the Matter case (the credential, not the whole user), same root cause.

## Why the asymmetry matters

The write path's worst case is that a mis-adopted user gets renamed and re-PINned — visible, and repaired by the next sync. The teardown path's worst case is the permanent deletion of a credential this integration never wrote, with no record of what was removed.

**Adoption belongs to the path that can repair a wrong guess.**

## Suggested fix

Resolve by tag only when releasing. A `scope` parameter on the shared resolution rather than a second resolver, so the two paths cannot drift and the release path does not quietly skip a repair the shared one gains later.

Worth a test per provider for "release a slot whose lock-side user was never created by LCM leaves foreign users alone".

## Provenance

Found by a review pass over #1514 (v6 → main). Confirmed pre-existing: `git show origin/main:custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/matter.py` has the same `async_release_managed_slot`, and v6's only change to `matter.py` is the six-line event-field removal.
EOF

content.text:
The provider review is in. **CI on #1514 is fully green**, and this round found the most serious bug of the session — but it isn't v6's.

**The finding: releasing a slot can delete a lock credential LCM never created.** Filed as **[#1518](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/issues/1518)** against `main`.

`async_release_managed_slot` resolves the user to delete using **find-or-adopt** — the same logic the *write* path uses. Matter's second lookup adopts any *untagged* user owning a PIN at `cred.slot == slot`, then `ClearUser` cascades to that user and all its credentials.

The reproduction is uncomfortably ordinary: homeowner adds a PIN via the manufacturer's app (untagged user, credential index 1) → you add "Guest" in LCM, who gets slot 1, and never give them a PIN → you delete "Guest". `pairs_removed` is derived purely from configuration, so the release fires for a slot that never held anything, adoption matches the homeowner's user, and it's gone. Nothing reports why that person is locked out. Two amplifiers: the loop runs for *every* lock in the entry, and a repeat release falls through to adoption again.

`_base.py` has the same shape one layer down — deletes the credential rather than the user, same root cause, and under Z-Wave User Credential CC `credential_index_follows_slot` makes the collision likely.

The asymmetry is the whole point: **adoption belongs to the path that can repair a wrong guess.** The write path's worst case is a rename that the next sync fixes; teardown's worst case is permanent.

**I did not bundle it into #1514.** I checked provenance rather than assuming: `async_release_managed_slot` and both fallbacks are on `main` today, and v6's only change to `matter.py` is the six-line event-field removal. It ships to users now, so it deserves its own fix on `main` with per-provider tests — not a quiet rider on a release PR.

**What was genuinely v6's — [#1517](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/1517):**

v6 converted three zwave_js notification tests to assert on a mocked `async_fire_code_slot_event`. That proves the decoding calls the funnel, but the funnel is deliberately silent for a slot no entry manages — which is exactly what those tests configure. So nothing proved a keypad press produces a `credential_used` event at all. Added one end-to-end test on the existing set-up fixture, asserting the payload names the **person**; offsetting the decoded `userId` fails it with `assert 'slot2' == 'slot1'`. Plus the dead `topic` parameter, last sibling of the `OPERATION_SOURCE_NAMES` constant.

The reviewer also verified the event removal was otherwise complete — no dangling references to any of the eight removed constants in code, comments, blueprints or shipped config, no provider lost data it still uses, and all seven `credential_used` fields are structurally guaranteed because every provider funnels through the base.

The frontend/websocket review is still running.

Verified: `EDIT VALUE after starting edit on a masked occupied slot: ""` with `_revealed: true`.

Also note this fires for `code_display: 'masked'` too — a card explicitly configured "Always Masked" still resubscribes with `reveal: true` and pulls every managed user's cleartext PIN over the websocket on the first edit click. Nothing renders it, but it is a card asking for what it was configured not to show.

content.subject: Add zero-lock availability guard in entity.py
content.description: _is_available currently returns any() over self.locks, so an entry with no locks makes every entity permanently unavailable. Guard so that an entry with no availability sources is available. Do NOT touch the per-lock override at entity.py:374 — those entities always have a lock.

Availability: no sources -> available; configured source going unavailable -> entities unavailable; source recovering -> available. Mutation-check the guard rather than trusting line coverage.

No Breaking Change section unless there is a real one. Then close #1494 and #1489 referencing the replacement.

content.subject: Fix #1491: reauth orphans a dropped lock's credential store
content.description: Reauth calls async_update_entry + async_reload, so a lock swapped out never gets the per-lock removal the options flow does: invoke_lock_removed_handlers, lock_dropped repair deletion, and async_unload_lock(remove_permanently=True). For VirtualLock the store IS the credentials, so a cleartext PIN outlives every entry referencing it. Repro test lands in tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py::TestReauthLockSwap. Fix must SHARE the listener's removal block, not duplicate it — a second path would skip the repair deletion exactly like the sibling-method bug. Note async_unload_lock no-ops when the lock instance is absent (runtime_data.locks.pop -> continue), which matters if the entry failed setup.

content.subject: Add set_credential / clear_credential actions (#1493)
content.description: Config-level, credential-typed actions: config_entry_id/title + name (matched by identity(), i.e. whitespace-normalized + casefolded) + credential_type, plus value for set. Route through SlotEntityCoordinator.async_request_pin_update rather than writing config directly — it is documented as the authoritative gate for both ends and carries whitespace stripping, per-lock length validation, and the disable-on-clear side effect. Gate credential_type on MANAGED_CREDENTIAL_TYPES (PIN only today). Also log a deprecation warning from set_usercode/clear_usercode pointing at the new pair, without changing their behavior.

content.subject: add_user/delete_user take lists (subentry step 3, shipped first)
content.description: add_user gains a `users` list field with ObjectSelector(multiple, fields, label_field); cv.ensure_list for a single dict; _flat_user_to_list normalizer BEFORE validation so the released flat shape still works. delete_user keeps `name`, wrapped in cv.ensure_list. All-or-nothing: validate every name, allocate ONCE for len(existing)+N, write ONCE. Pin with a test that both input shapes produce one allocation and one write. Non-breaking, so targets main.

content.subject: Subentry model move: EntryConfig reads subentries, v4→v5 migration, services write them
content.description: Steps 2+3 of the design, done together because the read and write must flip in one change or the entry has two disagreeing sources. EntryConfig.from_entry builds users/assignment from entry.subentries (subentry_type "user", title=name, data={slot,pin,enabled,condition}); migration v4->v5 creates subentries from users+slot_assignment and CLEARS the old keys; services use async_add_subentry/async_remove_subentry/async_update_subentry. EntryConfig's external surface (users, assignment, name_for, slot, has_slot) must not change — if callers above the config layer need edits, the abstraction leaked and that is worth knowing. Option A: keep slot_num in unique IDs, nothing renames.
